pratibha_layers.label: Practice (Abhyasa)
pratibha_layers.body: Read this passage slowly three times. Pause for one minute and write one sentence about how to apply it today.

items.citation: Bhagavad Gita — Renunciation Is Inner, Not Avoidant
items.resonance: Both texts locate renunciation not in withdrawal from the world but in a shift of inner stance toward it. Astavakra's recognition 'I am the ocean, not the waves' parallels the Gita's teaching that renunciation is relinquishing possessiveness *within* action—a cognitive reorientation that leaves the world intact while dissolving the agent's claim to it.
items.divergence: The Gita emphasizes duty and action as the field of renunciation, while Astavakra treats recognition of non-difference as itself the completion of renunciation, making action secondary or illusory.

items.citation: Tao Te Ching — The Paradox of Simplicity
items.resonance: Both teach that renunciation operates through negation of a false stance—Astavakra negates identification with the waves (the manifest multiplicity), while the Tao Te Ching negates 'sageness and wisdom' (constructed knowledge and ambition). Each sees the renounced state as a return to undifferentiated simplicity.
items.divergence: Astavakra grounds this negation in metaphysical non-duality (the wave is never separate from the ocean), whereas the Tao Te Ching emphasizes ethical and social benefit ('better for the people') as the fruit of simplicity.

title: The Crisis Before Clarity
sanskrit_devanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच कृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् ।
दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥ १.२८ ॥

सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ।
वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ १.२९ ॥

गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते ।
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥ १.३० ॥

निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव ।
न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥ १.३१ ॥

न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च ।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥ १.३२ ॥

येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च ।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥ १.३३ ॥

आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः ।
मातुलाः श्चशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥ १.३४ ॥

एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन ।
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥ १.३५ ॥

निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन ।
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥ १.३६ ॥

तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् ।
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥ १.३७ ॥

यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः ।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥ १.३८ ॥

कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् ।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥ १.३९ ॥

कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः ।
धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥ १.४० ॥

अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः ।
स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥ १.४१ ॥

सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च ।
पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥ १.४२ ॥

दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः ।
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥ १.४३ ॥

उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन ।
नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम ॥ १.४४ ॥

अर्जुन उवाच कृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् ।
दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥ १.२८ ॥

सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ।
वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ १.२९ ॥

गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते ।
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥ १.३० ॥

निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव ।
न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥ १.३१ ॥

न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च ।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥ १.३२ ॥

येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च ।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥ १.३३ ॥

आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः ।
मातुलाः श्चशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥ १.३४ ॥

एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन ।
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥ १.३५ ॥

निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन ।
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥ १.३६ ॥

तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् ।
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥ १.३७ ॥

यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः ।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥ १.३८ ॥

कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् ।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥ १.३९ ॥

कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः ।
धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥ १.४० ॥

अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः ।
स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥ १.४१ ॥

सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च ।
पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥ १.४२ ॥

दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः ।
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥ १.४३ ॥

उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन ।
नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम ॥ १.४४ ॥

अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् ।
यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ॥ १.४५ ॥

यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः ।
धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥ १.४६ ॥

सञ्जय उवाच एवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् ।
विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥ १.४७ ॥

title: Action Without Possessiveness
sanskrit_devanagari:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ २.४७ ॥

योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥ २.४८ ॥

दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय ।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥ २.४९ ॥

बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते ।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥ २.५० ॥
sanskrit_iast:
karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana |
mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi || 2.47 ||

yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya |
siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate || 2.48 ||

dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanañjaya |
buddhau śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ || 2.49 ||

buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte |
tasmādyogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam || 2.50 ||
translation_literal: You are responsible for action, not for ownership of outcome. When motive collapses into result-claiming, action becomes anxiety-management. Yoga here means steady offering of precise effort while relinquishing possessive identity over consequences.
commentary:
The claim is that bondage is produced less by action itself than by appropriation of action into egoic accounting. The counterintuitive move is that detachment in the Gita does not mean passivity; it means purified participation. Krishna does not permit Arjuna to retreat into inaction. He redefines freedom as non-possessive action at full intensity.

This distinction is foundational for karma-yoga. If one clings to fruit, one's nervous system becomes hostage to fluctuating conditions. If one renounces fruit while doing required work, action becomes a discipline of alignment rather than self-manufacture. Equanimity is therefore not emotional flatness; it is stability of orientation across gain and loss.

Existentially, this teaching is extraordinarily practical in performance-driven culture. Burnout, moral compromise, and reactive decision-making often come from fruit-fixation: reputation, control, outcome certainty. The Gita's remedy is not indifference but consecration: do what is right, as well as possible, for a truth greater than self-image. This shift preserves energy, sharpens judgment, and protects dignity under uncertainty. It also makes sustained service possible, because your identity no longer rises and falls with every external metric.

Key Terms:

**karma (कर्म)** - action/deed -> in this context, unavoidable participation in causal-moral life, not fate -> reducing to "destiny" obscures agency.

**phala (फल)** - fruit/result -> the appropriated payoff of action that binds identity when clung to -> "result" misses the psychological possessiveness implied.

**karma-yoga (कर्मयोग)** - yoga of action -> disciplined, non-possessive participation in duty -> "work ethic" is too shallow for its contemplative depth.

**samatva (समत्व)** - equanimity/evenness -> stable inner balance across success/failure -> not emotional numbness but regulated clarity.
insight: The claim is that bondage is produced less by action itself than by appropriation of action into egoic accounting.
practice: Choose one high-stakes task today and define success only as "full integrity of effort," not as external result.

सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥ २.४८ ॥

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Translation
pratibha_layers.body: You are responsible for action, not for ownership of outcome. When motive collapses into result-claiming, action becomes anxiety-management. Yoga here means steady offering of precise effort while relinquishing possessive identity over consequences.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body:
The claim is that bondage is produced less by action itself than by appropriation of action into egoic accounting. The counterintuitive move is that detachment in the Gita does not mean passivity; it means purified participation. Krishna does not permit Arjuna to retreat into inaction. He redefines freedom as non-possessive action at full intensity.

This distinction is foundational for karma-yoga. If one clings to fruit, one's nervous system becomes hostage to fluctuating conditions. If one renounces fruit while doing required work, action becomes a discipline of alignment rather than self-manufacture. Equanimity is therefore not emotional flatness; it is stability of orientation across gain and loss.

Existentially, this teaching is extraordinarily practical in performance-driven culture. Burnout, moral compromise, and reactive decision-making often come from fruit-fixation: reputation, control, outcome certainty. The Gita's remedy is not indifference but consecration: do what is right, as well as possible, for a truth greater than self-image. This shift preserves energy, sharpens judgment, and protects dignity under uncertainty. It also makes sustained service possible, because your identity no longer rises and falls with every external metric.

Key Terms:

**karma (कर्म)** - action/deed -> in this context, unavoidable participation in causal-moral life, not fate -> reducing to "destiny" obscures agency.

**phala (फल)** - fruit/result -> the appropriated payoff of action that binds identity when clung to -> "result" misses the psychological possessiveness implied.

**karma-yoga (कर्मयोग)** - yoga of action -> disciplined, non-possessive participation in duty -> "work ethic" is too shallow for its contemplative depth.

**samatva (समत्व)** - equanimity/evenness -> stable inner balance across success/failure -> not emotional numbness but regulated clarity.

yoga of action → disciplined, non-possessive participation in duty → "work ethic" is too shallow for its contemplative depth.
equanimity/evenness → stable inner balance across success/failure → not emotional numbness but regulated clarity.

items.resonance: Both insist on right action now without dependence on applause or guaranteed outcomes.
items.divergence: Marcus grounds in Stoic cosmopolis; Gita grounds in yoga, devotion, and dharma-theology.

items.resonance: Both show that releasing grasping at outcomes opens immediacy and finer attention.
items.divergence: VBT is technique-oriented phenomenology; Gita anchors in ethical action within social duty.

items.citation: Plato, Republic IV (justice as right order)
items.resonance: Both prioritize right ordering of inner motives over external reward metrics.
items.divergence: Plato frames civic-psychic harmony; Gita integrates action-renunciation and God-orientation.

pratibha_layers.body: Choose one high-stakes task today and define success only as "full integrity of effort," not as external result.

unit_label: Yajna as the Ecology of Action
title: Yajna as the Ecology of Action
sanskrit_devanagari:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः ।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर ॥ ३.९ ॥

सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः ।
अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥ ३.१० ॥

देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः ।
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥ ३.११ ॥

इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः ।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥ ३.१२ ॥

यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥ ३.१३ ॥

अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः ।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥ ३.१४ ॥

कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् ।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ ३.१५ ॥

एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः ।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥ ३.१६ ॥
sanskrit_iast:
yajñārthātkarmaṇo'nyatra loko'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ |
tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṃgaḥ samācara || 3.9 ||

sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ |
anena prasaviṣyadhvameṣa vo'stviṣṭakāmadhuk || 3.10 ||

devānbhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ |
parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha || 3.11 ||

iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ |
tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ || 3.12 ||

yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ |
bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt || 3.13 ||

annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ |
yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ || 3.14 ||

karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam |
tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam || 3.15 ||

evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ |
aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati || 3.16 ||
translation_literal: Action becomes binding when taken as private consumption; it becomes liberative when offered as yajna--reciprocal participation in the larger order that sustains all life. To live well is to contribute to the sustaining cycle, not merely extract from it.
commentary:
The claim is that ethics is cosmological before it is individual. Krishna's counterintuitive move is to present sacrifice not as ritual residue but as structural reciprocity: giving sustains receiving; receiving without offering corrupts person and world. The "wheel" image describes interdependence as law, not sentiment.

In karma-yoga terms, yajna dissolves isolated doership. You still act, but no longer as sovereign owner of process and product. Action becomes relational intelligence: each deed either nourishes or depletes the field in which all beings participate. This converts duty from burden into contribution.

Existentially, this teaching is urgently contemporary. Ecological crisis, social fragmentation, and organizational burnout all share a common pattern: extraction without reciprocity. The Gita's criterion is simple and difficult--does your work feed only your private ambition, or does it return nourishment to the network that enables your life? Yajna-consciousness recalibrates consumption, speech, labor, and attention. It also counters nihilism by showing that ordinary, disciplined contribution is spiritually significant. The sacred is not elsewhere; it is enacted in how you circulate value through the systems that hold you.

Key Terms:

**yajna (यज्ञ)** - sacrificial offering -> in this passage, reciprocal participation in sustaining order, not only altar-ritual -> reducing to "ritual sacrifice" narrows the doctrine.

**loka-sangraha (लोकसंग्रह)** - holding the world together -> action for collective stability and uplift -> default "public service" misses metaphysical scope.

**rta (ऋत)** - cosmic order/truth-order -> implied background of reciprocal process -> absent this, yajna appears merely transactional.

**bandha (बन्ध)** - bondage -> the enchainment produced by self-centered action patterns -> not external punishment but structural consequence.
insight: The claim is that ethics is cosmological before it is individual.
practice: Before beginning work, state in one sentence: "Who beyond me is served by this action?" and adjust one step to make that true.

title: Knowledge Burns Ownership
sanskrit_devanagari:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः ।
स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥ ४.१८ ॥

यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः ।
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥ ४.१९ ॥

त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः ।
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥ ४.२० ॥

निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः ।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ ४.२१ ॥

यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः ।
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥ ४.२२ ॥

गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः ।
यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥ ४.२३ ॥

ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् ।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥ ४.२४ ॥

यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन ।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥ ४.३७ ॥

न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥ ४.३८ ॥

श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः ।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ४.३९ ॥
sanskrit_iast:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ |
sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt || 4.18 ||

yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ |
jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ || 4.19 ||

tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ |
karmaṇyabhipravṛtto'pi naiva kiñcitkaroti saḥ || 4.20 ||

nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ |
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam || 4.21 ||

yadṛcchālābhasantuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ |
samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate || 4.22 ||

gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ |
yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate || 4.23 ||

brahmārpaṇaṃ brahmahavirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam |
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā || 4.24 ||

yathaidhāṃsi samiddho'gnirbhasmasātkurute'rjuna |
jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā || 4.37 ||

na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitramiha vidyate |
tatsvayaṃ yogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati || 4.38 ||

śraddhāvām̐llabhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ |
jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntimacireṇādhigacchati || 4.39 ||
translation_literal: True knowing alters the ontology of action. When the actor-identity is seen as provisional, compulsive ownership weakens. Action continues, but its binding residue burns in the fire of discernment.
commentary:
The claim is that liberation requires epistemic transformation, not only ethical effort. The counterintuitive move is to say that one can be fully active yet inwardly non-acting when egoic appropriation has ceased. This is not metaphysical wordplay; it is a shift in where agency is claimed from.

Chapter 4 deepens karma-yoga into jnana-yoga. Krishna reframes sacrifice itself as knowledge-process: actor, offering, fire, and recipient can all be seen as Brahmanic expressions within one field. When this vision stabilizes, karma no longer deposits the same binding imprint because "I, the separate owner" is no longer central.

Existentially, this teaching addresses the fatigue of chronic self-authorship. Modern identity is often overburdened by the demand to curate and defend a private self in every act. Knowledge, in the Gita's sense, is release from this over-tightened center. One still fulfills obligations, but with less narcissistic friction and less fear-driven control. The practical sign is lighter action with greater precision: you do what is needed without turning each deed into a referendum on your worth. That is why knowledge purifies--it interrupts the loop that keeps karmic anxiety self-renewing.

Key Terms:

**jnana (ज्ञान)** - liberating knowledge -> direct discernment of reality's structure, not mere information -> "knowledge" as data misses transformative force.

**akarma (अकर्म)** - non-action -> not inactivity, but non-binding interior stance within action -> literal inactivity reading distorts the teaching.

**karma-bandha (कर्मबन्ध)** - bondage through action -> cumulative binding effect of appropriated doership -> more than "consequence"; it is identity-level entanglement.

**brahmarpana (ब्रह्मार्पण)** - offering as Brahman -> sacrificial frame where offering-process is seen as non-separate -> translation as generic "offering" loses metaphysical point.
insight: The claim is that liberation requires epistemic transformation, not only ethical effort.
practice: During one repeated task today, silently replace "I am doing this" with "this is being done through this body-mind" and observe the shift.

pratibha_layers.body:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः ।
स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥ ४.१८ ॥

यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः ।
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥ ४.१९ ॥

त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः ।
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥ ४.२० ॥

निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः ।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ ४.२१ ॥

यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः ।
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥ ४.२२ ॥

गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः ।
यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥ ४.२३ ॥

ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् ।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥ ४.२४ ॥

यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन ।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥ ४.३७ ॥

न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥ ४.३८ ॥

श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः ।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ४.३९ ॥

pratibha_layers.body:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ |
sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt || 4.18 ||

yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ |
jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ || 4.19 ||

tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ |
karmaṇyabhipravṛtto'pi naiva kiñcitkaroti saḥ || 4.20 ||

nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ |
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam || 4.21 ||

yadṛcchālābhasantuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ |
samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate || 4.22 ||

gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ |
yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate || 4.23 ||

brahmārpaṇaṃ brahmahavirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam |
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā || 4.24 ||

yathaidhāṃsi samiddho'gnirbhasmasātkurute'rjuna |
jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā || 4.37 ||

na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitramiha vidyate |
tatsvayaṃ yogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati || 4.38 ||

śraddhāvām̐llabhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ |
jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntimacireṇādhigacchati || 4.39 ||

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Translation
pratibha_layers.body: True knowing alters the ontology of action. When the actor-identity is seen as provisional, compulsive ownership weakens. Action continues, but its binding residue burns in the fire of discernment.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body:
The claim is that liberation requires epistemic transformation, not only ethical effort. The counterintuitive move is to say that one can be fully active yet inwardly non-acting when egoic appropriation has ceased. This is not metaphysical wordplay; it is a shift in where agency is claimed from.

Chapter 4 deepens karma-yoga into jnana-yoga. Krishna reframes sacrifice itself as knowledge-process: actor, offering, fire, and recipient can all be seen as Brahmanic expressions within one field. When this vision stabilizes, karma no longer deposits the same binding imprint because "I, the separate owner" is no longer central.

Existentially, this teaching addresses the fatigue of chronic self-authorship. Modern identity is often overburdened by the demand to curate and defend a private self in every act. Knowledge, in the Gita's sense, is release from this over-tightened center. One still fulfills obligations, but with less narcissistic friction and less fear-driven control. The practical sign is lighter action with greater precision: you do what is needed without turning each deed into a referendum on your worth. That is why knowledge purifies--it interrupts the loop that keeps karmic anxiety self-renewing.

Key Terms:

**jnana (ज्ञान)** - liberating knowledge -> direct discernment of reality's structure, not mere information -> "knowledge" as data misses transformative force.

**akarma (अकर्म)** - non-action -> not inactivity, but non-binding interior stance within action -> literal inactivity reading distorts the teaching.

**karma-bandha (कर्मबन्ध)** - bondage through action -> cumulative binding effect of appropriated doership -> more than "consequence"; it is identity-level entanglement.

**brahmarpana (ब्रह्मार्पण)** - offering as Brahman -> sacrificial frame where offering-process is seen as non-separate -> translation as generic "offering" loses metaphysical point.

items.definition: non-action → not inactivity, but non-binding interior stance within action → literal inactivity reading distorts the teaching.
bondage through action → cumulative binding effect of appropriated doership → more than "consequence"; it is identity-level entanglement.
offering as Brahman → sacrificial frame where offering-process is seen as non-separate → translation as generic "offering" loses metaphysical point.

items.resonance: Both move from surface mechanics toward deeper explanatory principles that reframe agency.
items.divergence: *Phaedo* builds dialectical-metaphysical proof; Gita integrates insight with devotional action discipline.

items.citation: Vijnana Bhairava Tantra 74 (awareness in all acts)
items.resonance: Both teach that action can be transfigured by recognition of deeper consciousness-field.
items.divergence: VBT gives direct contemplative triggers; Gita situates in ethical-duty and lineage context.

items.resonance: Both depict higher knowledge as burning prior ignorance and freeing one from binding effects.
items.divergence: Mundaka emphasizes renunciant knowledge path; Gita fuses knowledge with engaged action.

pratibha_layers.label: Practice (Abhyasa)
pratibha_layers.body: During one repeated task today, silently replace "I am doing this" with "this is being done through this body-mind" and observe the shift.

title: Renunciation Is Inner, Not Avoidant
sanskrit_devanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि ।
यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्िचतम् ॥ ५.१ ॥

श्री भगवानुवाच संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ ।
तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥ ५.२ ॥

ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ ५.३ ॥

सांख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः ।
एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥ ५.४ ॥

यत्सांख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते ।
एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥ ५.५ ॥

संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः ।
योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ५.६ ॥

योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः ।
सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥ ५.७ ॥

नैव किंचित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् ।
पश्यन् श्रृणवन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन् श्वसन् ॥ ५.८ ॥

प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन् ॥ ५.९ ॥

ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः ।
लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥ ५.१० ॥

कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि ।
योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये ॥ ५.११ ॥

युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् ।
अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥ ५.१२ ॥
sanskrit_iast:
arjuna uvāca saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punaryogaṃ ca śaṃsasi |
yacchreya etayorekaṃ tanme brūhi suniśिcatam || 5.1 ||

śrī bhagavānuvāca saṃnyāsaḥ karmayogaśca niḥśreyasakarāvubhau |
tayostu karmasaṃnyāsātkarmayogo viśiṣyate || 5.2 ||

jñeyaḥ sa nityasaṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati |
nirdvandvo hi mahābāho sukhaṃ bandhātpramucyate || 5.3 ||

sāṃkhyayogau pṛthagbālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ |
ekamapyāsthitaḥ samyagubhayorvindate phalam || 5.4 ||

yatsāṃkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tadyogairapi gamyate |
ekaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati || 5.5 ||

saṃnyāsastu mahābāho duḥkhamāptumayogataḥ |
yogayukto munirbrahma nacireṇādhigacchati || 5.6 ||

yogayukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ |
sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā kurvannapi na lipyate || 5.7 ||

naiva kiṃcitkaromīti yukto manyeta tattvavit |
paśyan śrṛṇavanspṛśañjighrannaśnangacchansvapan śvasan || 5.8 ||

pralapanvisṛjangṛhṇannunmiṣannimiṣannapi |
indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan || 5.9 ||

brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ |
lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatramivāmbhasā || 5.10 ||

kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalairindriyairapi |
yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvā''tmaśuddhaye || 5.11 ||

yuktaḥ karmaphalaṃ tyaktvā śāntimāpnoti naiṣṭhikīm |
ayuktaḥ kāmakāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate || 5.12 ||
translation_literal: Renunciation is fulfilled not by fleeing action but by relinquishing possessiveness within action. The mature practitioner remains in life-process while unstuck from egoic claim, moving like a lotus leaf in water--in contact, not contaminated.
commentary:
The claim is that outer withdrawal is secondary to inner non-clinging. The counterintuitive move is explicit: Krishna affirms both renunciation and disciplined action, yet privileges action-with-detachment for most practitioners. This prevents spirituality from becoming avoidance.

Chapter 5 resolves a perennial confusion: if bondage arises through action, should one stop acting? Krishna's answer is diagnostic. Bondage does not come from movement itself; it comes from attachment, aversion, and ownership. Therefore one may remain fully engaged while becoming progressively unstained. Renunciation is transposed from geography to interior architecture.

Existentially, this is liberating for householders and professionals. Many assume spiritual depth demands total external exit; others use "engagement" to excuse compulsive ambition. The Gita rejects both distortions. It asks for rigorous inward relinquishment while maintaining responsible participation in relational life. The lotus metaphor is not passivity--it is disciplined permeability without psychic soaking. You can serve, decide, lead, and labor while reducing ego-residue. Over time, this produces both ethical steadiness and psychological lightness.

Key Terms:

**sannyasa (संन्यास)** - renunciation -> in this chapter, relinquishment of possessive self-claim, not mere social withdrawal -> simplistic "monasticism" reading is incomplete.

**tyaga (त्याग)** - letting-go/abandonment -> practical release of fruit-ownership and egoic insistence -> "sacrifice" without interiority misses operative meaning.

**yukta (युक्त)** - integrated/yoked -> the practitioner inwardly joined and therefore balanced in action -> "disciplined" alone is too thin.

**asanga (असङ्ग)** - non-attachment -> contact without clinging or contamination -> not indifference but relational freedom.
insight: The claim is that outer withdrawal is secondary to inner non-clinging.
practice: Complete one unavoidable duty today while repeating: "Engaged fully, owning lightly"; notice where grasping enters and soften it once.

sanskrit_devanagari:
योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः ।
एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥ ६.१० ॥

शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः ।
नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम् ॥ ६.११ ॥

तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः ।
उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये ॥ ६.१२ ॥

समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः ।
संप्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥ ६.१३ ॥

प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः ।
मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥ ६.१४ ॥

युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः ।
शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥ ६.१५ ॥

नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः ।
न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥ ६.१६ ॥

युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु ।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥ ६.१७ ॥

यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते ।
निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥ ६.१८ ॥

यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ।
योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥ ६.१९ ॥

यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया ।
यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥ ६.२० ॥

सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् ।
वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥ ६.२१ ॥

यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः ।
यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥ ६.२२ ॥

तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् ।
स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥ ६.२३ ॥

सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः ।
मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥ ६.२४ ॥

शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया ।
आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥ ६.२५ ॥

यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् ।
ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥ ६.२६ ॥

चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् ।
तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥ ६.३४ ॥

श्री भगवानुवाच असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं ।
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥ ६.३५ ॥

असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः ।
वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥ ६.३६ ॥

translation_literal: Yoga-mastery is iterative, not dramatic: establish body, regulate habit, and repeatedly return attention from dispersion to center. The mind's restlessness is acknowledged, not denied; discipline is defined as return, again and again, through practice and detachment.
commentary:
The claim is that contemplative stability is trainable through rhythm, not force. Krishna's counterintuitive move is pastoral realism: he fully agrees with Arjuna that the mind is difficult, then denies that difficulty is disqualification. The path is abhyasa (repeated training) plus vairagya (degrasping), not heroic suppression.

This chapter prevents two common errors. First: romanticizing meditation as immediate transcendence. Second: pathologizing distraction as failure. In the Gita's view, each return of attention is itself yoga-act. Mastery grows by accumulated non-dramatic corrections. Even bodily instructions (seat, posture, moderation) are not peripheral; they scaffold subtle work by reducing friction in the psycho-physical system.

Existentially, this teaching is urgently applicable in attention-fragmented life. Digital overstimulation makes wandering mind feel normal and unchangeable. Krishna's prescription remains exact: simplify conditions, regulate consumption, and train return without self-hatred. Over time, this produces not only meditative calm but functional resilience: less impulsive speech, fewer identity hijacks, and greater availability to right action. Inner governance becomes possible because one stops demanding perfect focus and instead becomes faithful to deliberate return.

Key Terms:

**abhyasa (अभ्यास)** - sustained practice/repetition -> disciplined returning, not occasional inspiration -> "practice" without continuity misses its force.

**vairagya (वैराग्य)** - dispassion/degrasping -> release of compulsive pull, enabling attentional freedom -> "detachment" can sound cold if divorced from clarity.

**yoga (योग)** - yoking/integration -> unified alignment of body, mind, and higher orientation -> not merely posture or relaxation technique.

**atma-vinigraha (आत्मविनिग्रह)** - self-governance -> active regulation of inner movement toward steadiness -> weaker than "self-control" if reduced to repression.
insight: The claim is that contemplative stability is trainable through rhythm, not force.
practice: Set a 7-minute sit today: each time attention wanders, label it "wandering," return to breath once, and continue without self-critique.

items.divergence: Sutra tradition systematizes citta-vritti cessation; Gita embeds the same dynamic in devotion and duty ethics.

items.resonance: Both use repeated return to a subtle anchor to interrupt mental drift.
items.divergence: VBT offers short direct-entry methods; Gita frames a broader integrated discipline.

items.resonance: Both normalize mind-drift and insist on immediate return to governing principle.
items.divergence: Stoic return centers logos-duty; Gita unites return with yogic absorption and Krishna-refuge.

pratibha_layers.label: Practice (Abhyasa)
pratibha_layers.body: Set a 7-minute sit today: each time attention wanders, label it "wandering," return to breath once, and continue without self-critique.

पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ ।
जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ॥ ७.९ ॥

बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् ।
बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥ ७.१० ॥

बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्जितम् ।
धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥ ७.११ ॥

ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये ।
मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥ ७.१२ ॥

अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः ।
अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥ १०.२० ॥

आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् ।
मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी ॥ १०.२१ ॥

वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः ।
इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥ १०.२२ ॥

रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् ।
वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् ॥ १०.२३ ॥

पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् ।
सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥ १०.२४ ॥

महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् ।
यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः ॥ १०.२५ ॥

अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः ।
गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः ॥ १०.२६ ॥

उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् ।
ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् ॥ १०.२७ ॥

आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् ।
प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः ॥ १०.२८ ॥

अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् ।
पितृ़णामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् ॥ १०.२९ ॥

प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् ।
मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् ॥ १०.३० ॥

पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् ।
झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी ॥ १०.३१ ॥

सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन ।
अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् ॥ १०.३२ ॥

अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च ।
अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः ॥ १०.३३ ॥

मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् ।
कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥ १०.३४ ॥

बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् ।
मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः ॥ १०.३५ ॥

द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ।
जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् ॥ १०.३६ ॥

वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनंजयः ।
मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः ॥ १०.३७ ॥

दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् ।
मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् ॥ १०.३८ ॥

यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन ।
न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् ॥ १०.३९ ॥

नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप ।
एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया ॥ १०.४० ॥

यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा ।
तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम् ॥ १०.४१ ॥

raso'hamapsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśisūryayoḥ |
praṇavaḥ sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu || 7.8 ||

puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca tejaścāsmi vibhāvasau |
jīvanaṃ sarvabhūteṣu tapaścāsmi tapasviṣu || 7.9 ||

bījaṃ māṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam |
buddhirbuddhimatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham || 7.10 ||

balaṃ balavatāṃ cāhaṃ kāmarāgavivarjitam |
dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo'smi bharatarṣabha || 7.11 ||

ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasāstāmasāśca ye |
matta eveti tānviddhi natvahaṃ teṣu te mayi || 7.12 ||

ahamātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ |
ahamādiśca madhyaṃ ca bhūtānāmanta eva ca || 10.20 ||

ādityānāmahaṃ viṣṇurjyotiṣāṃ raviraṃśumān |
marīcirmarutāmasmi nakṣatrāṇāmahaṃ śaśī || 10.21 ||

vedānāṃ sāmavedo'smi devānāmasmi vāsavaḥ |
indriyāṇāṃ manaścāsmi bhūtānāmasmi cetanā || 10.22 ||

rudrāṇāṃ śaṅkaraścāsmi vitteśo yakṣarakṣasām |
vasūnāṃ pāvakaścāsmi meruḥ śikhariṇāmaham || 10.23 ||

purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ māṃ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim |
senānīnāmahaṃ skandaḥ sarasāmasmi sāgaraḥ || 10.24 ||

maharṣīṇāṃ bhṛgurahaṃ girāmasmyekamakṣaram |
yajñānāṃ japayajño'smi sthāvarāṇāṃ himālayaḥ || 10.25 ||

aśvatthaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ |
gandharvāṇāṃ citrarathaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo muniḥ || 10.26 ||

uccaiḥśravasamaśvānāṃ viddhi māmamṛtodbhavam |
airāvataṃ gajendrāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca narādhipam || 10.27 ||

āyudhānāmahaṃ vajraṃ dhenūnāmasmi kāmadhuk |
prajanaścāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇāmasmi vāsukiḥ || 10.28 ||

anantaścāsmi nāgānāṃ varuṇo yādasāmaham |
pitṛ़ṇāmaryamā cāsmi yamaḥ saṃyamatāmaham || 10.29 ||

prahlādaścāsmi daityānāṃ kālaḥ kalayatāmaham |
mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛgendro'haṃ vainateyaśca pakṣiṇām || 10.30 ||

pavanaḥ pavatāmasmi rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāmaham |
jhaṣāṇāṃ makaraścāsmi srotasāmasmi jāhnavī || 10.31 ||

sargāṇāmādirantaśca madhyaṃ caivāhamarjuna |
adhyātmavidyā vidyānāṃ vādaḥ pravadatāmaham || 10.32 ||

akṣarāṇāmakāro'smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya ca |
ahamevākṣayaḥ kālo dhātā'haṃ viśvatomukhaḥ || 10.33 ||

mṛtyuḥ sarvaharaścāhamudbhavaśca bhaviṣyatām |
kīrtiḥ śrīrvākca nārīṇāṃ smṛtirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā || 10.34 ||

bṛhatsāma tathā sāmnāṃ gāyatrī chandasāmaham |
māsānāṃ mārgaśīrṣo'hamṛtūnāṃ kusumākaraḥ || 10.35 ||

dyūtaṃ chalayatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham |
jayo'smi vyavasāyo'smi sattvaṃ sattvavatāmaham || 10.36 ||

vṛṣṇīnāṃ vāsudevo'smi pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ |
munīnāmapyahaṃ vyāsaḥ kavīnāmuśanā kaviḥ || 10.37 ||

daṇḍo damayatāmasmi nītirasmi jigīṣatām |
maunaṃ caivāsmi guhyānāṃ jñānaṃ jñānavatāmaham || 10.38 ||

yaccāpi sarvabhūtānāṃ bījaṃ tadahamarjuna |
na tadasti vinā yatsyānmayā bhūtaṃ carācaram || 10.39 ||

nānto'sti mama divyānāṃ vibhūtīnāṃ paraṃtapa |
eṣa tūddeśataḥ prokto vibhūtervistaro mayā || 10.40 ||

yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā |
tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejoṃ'śasaṃbhavam || 10.41 ||
translation_literal: Krishna discloses that the sacred is not elsewhere. The field of encounter with the Supreme includes water, light, courage, intelligence, and excellence itself. Vibhuti (विभूति) is not spectacle alone; it is the recognition that every genuine radiance in experience is a disclosure of the One.
commentary:
The claim is that metaphysical non-duality must become perceptual devotion. The counterintuitive move is that Krishna does not begin with abstract transcendence alone; he trains Arjuna's seeing through concrete excellences: taste, luminosity, vitality, intelligence, moral force. In doing so, he re-educates perception. The world is no longer inert object-field; it is vibhuti-field--a patterned unveiling of the Divine.

This chapter-arc prevents both materialism and escapist spirituality. Materialism reduces excellence to mechanism; escapism flees the manifest world in search of a distant absolute. Krishna rejects both by teaching immanence-with-transcendence: all glories arise from Him, yet He is not exhausted by any finite manifestation. The spiritual task is therefore discernment, not denial.

Existentially, this teaching heals spiritual alienation. Many practitioners divide life into "sacred moments" and "ordinary time." Gita dissolves that split. If awareness is trained rightly, integrity in work, lucidity in thought, beauty in art, and courage under pressure become contemplative gateways. This does not sacralize ego-achievement; it relativizes it. You do not worship success; you perceive the Source shining through transient forms. The result is gratitude without possession and reverence without superstition.

Key Terms:

**vibhuti (विभूति)** - divine manifestation/excellence -> specific modes in which the Supreme becomes perceptible in the manifest world -> translating as "power" alone misses revelatory function.

**ishvara (ईश्वर)** - Lord/Supreme Governor -> here the One who pervades all while transcending all forms -> "god" without this simultaneity is too thin.

**vasudeva (वासुदेव)** - name/title of Krishna as all-pervading Divine -> "all is Vasudeva" signals ontological unity-in-manifestation -> reading as sectarian label alone narrows it.

**prakriti (प्रकृति)** - Nature's matrix -> manifest qualities arise through prakriti, but their ground is the Supreme -> "nature" without metaphysical context can mislead.
insight: The claim is that metaphysical non-duality must become perceptual devotion.
practice: Identify three moments of excellence today (clarity, courage, beauty) and consciously name each: "This too is vibhuti (विभूति), not mine."
