agne naya supatha raye asman visvani deva vayunani vidvan |
yuyodhy asmaj juhuranam eno bhuyistham te nama uktim vidhema || 18 ||

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Translation
pratibha_layers.body: O Fire, lead us by the good path, knowing all our ways; remove crooked sin from us. We offer reverence.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body:
The text ends as ethical prayer: guidance, purification, humility.

Key Terms:

**supatha** - good path; **yuyodhi** - remove, ward off.

items.definition: good path → Agni asked to lead by the right way → trap: moralistic highway only; includes knowing our crookedness
crooked sin → to be removed by Fire’s knowing → trap: legal guilt alone
O Fire → knower of all ways as purifier → trap: elemental fire worship without ethical request

pratibha_layers.label: Practice (Abhyasa)
pratibha_layers.body: Close each day with one sincere request for clearer conduct tomorrow.

items.resonance: Both texts treat mantra as a dual practice: utterance paired with contemplative attention to meaning. The Isavasya prayer invokes Fire while requesting guidance; Patañjali's sutra joins repetition of the word with meditation on its sense—each binding vocalization to inner understanding.
items.divergence: The Upanishad frames mantra as ethical petition to a divine agent (Fire); Patañjali treats it as a technical method for stabilizing mind without invoking external agency.

items.citation: Svetasvatara Upanishad — Fire by Friction, Self by Om
items.resonance: Both use fire as a metaphor for latent spiritual power requiring proper means to manifest. The Isavasya addresses Fire as guide and purifier; the Svetasvatara describes the Self as fire hidden in wood, brought forth 'by the right means'—each posits a dormant force activated through correct practice.
items.divergence: The Isavasya frames fire as an external divine power to petition; the Svetasvatara locates fire as the Self's intrinsic nature, requiring technique rather than prayer.

items.resonance: Both assert that mantra operates through embodied realization, not mere conceptual knowledge. The Isavasya's prayer seeks actual purification and guidance (not just intellectual assent); the Siva Sutra states 'Knowledge becomes embodied reality'—each insists mantra's efficacy lies in lived transformation.
items.divergence: The Isavasya emphasizes ethical purification through divine grace; the Siva Sutra emphasizes non-dual recognition where knowledge and reality collapse into identity.

title: God Alone Contains All Temporal Distinctions
thesis: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.
source_excerpt: Praise belongs to God, before whose oneness there is no before unless the before is He and after whose singleness there is no after unless the after is He. He is, and there is not with Him any before or after, above or below, closeness or distance, how or where or when, time or moment or duration, manifested existence or place.
translation_literal: Praise belongs to God, before whose oneness there is no before unless the before is He and after whose singleness there is no after unless the after is He. He is, and there is not with Him any before or after, above or below, closeness or distance, how or where or when, time or moment or duration, manifested existence or place.
commentary: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.
practice: Read this passage slowly three times. Pause for one minute and write one sentence about how to apply it today.
sanskrit_devanagari:
الحمد لله الذي لم يكن قبل وحدانيته قبلُ إلا والقبل هو، ولم يكن بعد فردانيَّته بَعْدُ إلا والبَعْد هو. كان ولا بَعْد معه ولا قبل، ولا فوق ولا تحت، ولا قُرْب ولا بُعْد، ولا كيف، ولا أين ولا حين، ولا أوان ولا وقت ولا زمان، ولا كون ولا مكان، وهو الآن كما كان.

هو الواحد بلا وحدانية، وهو الفرد بلا فردانية. ليس مركَّبًا من الاسم والمسمَّى: هو الأول بلا أولية وهو الآخِر بلا آخِرية، وهو الظاهر بلا ظاهرية وهو الباطن بلا باطنية؛ أعني أنه هو وجود حروف "الأول" وهو وجود حروف "الآخِر"، وهو وجود حروف "الباطن" وهو وجود حروف "الظاهر". فلا أول ولا آخِر ولا ظاهر ولا باطن إلا وهو بلا صيران. هذه الحروف وجوده، وصيران وجوده هذه الحروف. – فافهم هذا لئلا تقع في غلط الحلولية.
sanskrit_iast:
al-ḥamdu lil-lāh alladhī lam yakun qabla waḥdāniyyatih qablu illā wal-qabl huwa, walam yakun baʿda fardāniyyatih baʿdu illā wal-baʿd huwa. kāna walā baʿd maʿahu walā qabla, walā fawqa walā taḥta, walā qurb walā buʿd, walā kayfa, walā ayna walā ḥayna, walā awān walā waqt walā zamān, walā kawn walā makān, wa huwa al-ān kamā kāna.

huwa al-wāḥid bilā waḥdāniyya, wa huwa al-fard bilā fardāniyya. laysa murakkaban min al-ism wal-masmā: huwa al-awwal bilā awwaliyya wa huwa al-ākhir bilā ākhiriyya, wa huwa al-ẓāhir bilā ẓāhiriyya wa huwa al-bāṭin bilā bāṭiniyya; aʿnī annahu huwa wujūd ḥurūf "al-awwal" wa huwa wujūd ḥurūf "al-ākhir", wa huwa wujūd ḥurūf "al-bāṭin" wa huwa wujūd ḥurūf "al-ẓāhir". fa-lā awwal walā ākhir walā ẓāhir walā bāṭin illā wa huwa bilā ṣayrān. hādhihi al-ḥurūf wujūdhu, wa ṣayrān wujūdhu hādhihi al-ḥurūf. – fafham hādhā li-allā taqaʿ fī ghalṭ al-ḥulūliyya.

pratibha_layers.body: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.

items.definition: Arabic tawḥīd from waḥḥada ‘to make/declare one’ → absolute oneness of the Real, radicalized here as sole agency and sole being Here: God Alone Contains All Temporal Distinctions Pearl #1 Praise belongs to God, before whose oneness there is no before unless the before is He and after whose si… Trap: hearing a creedal slogan rather than ontological exclusivity of wujūd

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: He is, and there is not with Him any before or after, above or below, closeness or distance, how or where or when, time or moment or duration, manifested exist… Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

Arabic third-person ‘He’ → the Real indicated beyond naming; deixis that refuses captive definition Here: He is, and there is not with Him any before or after, above or below, closeness or distance, how or where or when, time or moment or duration, manifested exist… Trap: hearing a mere pronoun rather than apophatic pointing

title: Beyond All Distinction, Always Present

huwa al-wāḥid bilā waḥdāniyya, wa huwa al-fard bilā fardāniyya. laysa murakkaban min al-ism wal-masmā: huwa al-awwal bilā awwaliyya wa huwa al-ākhir bilā ākhiriyya, wa huwa al-ẓāhir bilā ẓāhiriyya wa huwa al-bāṭin bilā bāṭiniyya; aʿnī annahu huwa wujūd ḥurūf "al-awwal" wa huwa wujūd ḥurūf "al-ākhir", wa huwa wujūd ḥurūf "al-bāṭin" wa huwa wujūd ḥurūf "al-ẓāhir". fa-lā awwal walā ākhir walā ẓāhir walā bāṭin illā wa huwa bilā ṣayrān. hādhihi al-ḥurūf wujūdhu, wa ṣayrān wujūdhu hādhihi al-ḥurūf. – fafham hādhā li-allā taqaʿ fī ghalṭ al-ḥulūliyya.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Translation
pratibha_layers.body: He is, and there is not with Him any before or after, above or below, closeness or distance, how or where or when, time or moment or duration, manifested existence or place. And He is now as He has always been. He is the one without oneness and the single without singleness.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.

items.definition: Arabic tawḥīd from waḥḥada ‘to make/declare one’ → absolute oneness of the Real, radicalized here as sole agency and sole being Here: He is the one without oneness and the single without singleness. Trap: hearing a creedal slogan rather than ontological exclusivity of wujūd

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: Beyond All Distinction, Always Present Pearl #2 He is, and there is not with Him any before or after, above or below, closeness or distance, how or where or wh… Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

‘self/soul/breath’ → the claiming self that must be known so its independence can be seen through Here: The next time you catch yourself saying "before" or "after," "here" or "there," pause on the word and whisper the line "He is now as He was," letting the disti… Trap: psychologizing as ego-therapy without ontological stakes

Arabic third-person ‘He’ → the Real indicated beyond naming; deixis that refuses captive definition Here: Beyond All Distinction, Always Present Pearl #2 He is, and there is not with Him any before or after, above or below, closeness or distance, how or where or wh… Trap: hearing a mere pronoun rather than apophatic pointing

items.citation: Mandukya Upanishad and Gaudapada Karika — Verse 12 · The Silence — Turīya as Amātrā
items.resonance: Both texts negate all relational and temporal categories (before/after, measure, phenomena) to point toward a fourth state that transcends dualistic experience. The Sufi passage strips away spatial-temporal predicates; the Upanishadic passage names Turīya as 'without measure' and 'cessation of phenomena'—both using systematic negation to disclose what remains.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi emphasizes divine transcendence and the absolute unity of God's being; Gaudapada locates this fourth state as the Self (Ātman), accessible through contemplative recognition rather than theological assertion.

items.resonance: Both passages describe a radical removal or stripping away—of relational predicates in the Sufi text, of 'coverings of knowledge' in the Yoga Sūtra—leaving what is almost nothing or nearly unknowable. The move is one of subtraction toward a residual, irreducible awareness.
items.divergence: Patañjali frames this as the final fruit of yogic practice (kaivalya); Ibn Arabi presents it as the eternal nature of divine being, not an achievement but a recognition of what always is.

items.resonance: Both use spatial metaphor (space/pot, infinite container and finite content) to dissolve subject-object duality and reveal the Self as boundless ground. The structure inverts ordinary perception: the world becomes small within consciousness, not consciousness within the world.
items.divergence: Astavakra employs the metaphor to teach non-dual realization of the individual self; Ibn Arabi's negation serves to isolate divine transcendence beyond all spatial or relational categories whatsoever.

title: Knowledge Turns From Object To Knower
thesis: The emphasis turns inward: clarity grows when attention returns to the knower rather than the passing content.
source_excerpt: Understand this so as not to make the mistake of those who believe in incarnation. He is not in anything and no thing is in Him, whether entering into Him or coming out of Him. It is in this way that you should know Him and not through theoretical knowledge, reason, understanding or conjecture, nor with the senses, the external eye or interior sight or perception. No one sees Him except Himself, no one reaches Him except Himself and no one knows Him except Himself.

pratibha_layers.label: Practice (Abhyasa)
pratibha_layers.body: Read this passage slowly three times. Pause for one minute and write one sentence about how to apply it today.

items.resonance: Both texts locate knowledge in the quality and direction of attention itself: Ibn Arabi's inward turn of attention to the knower (not the known) structurally mirrors the Śiva Sūtra's equation of sustained attention with knowledge as the primary epistemic act.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi emphasizes attention as a corrective against false metaphysical belief (incarnation), while the Śiva Sūtra presents attention as the fundamental ontological principle through which consciousness knows itself.

items.resonance: Both passages identify ignorance as a failure of self-recognition: Ibn Arabi warns against mistaking external content for the knower, while the Pratyabhijñā describes bewilderment as forgetting one's own authorship—both locate error in a collapse of reflexive awareness.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi frames this as a corrective epistemological move (understanding to avoid error), whereas Pratyabhijñā frames it as metaphysical bondage (ignorance of one's creative power as the Self).

items.citation: Tao Te Ching — Learning Adds; the Way Subtracts
items.resonance: Both texts prescribe a reversal of ordinary mental direction: Ibn Arabi's inward turn away from passing content parallels the Tao Te Ching's daily diminishment—both describe knowledge as a subtraction or withdrawal rather than accumulation.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi's withdrawal targets the knower's self-recognition within a theistic framework, while the Taoist diminishment aims at alignment with the impersonal Way through the negation of conceptual overlay.

pratibha_layers.body: Read this passage slowly three times. Pause for one minute and write one sentence about how to apply it today.

items.resonance: Both texts locate knowledge in the quality and direction of attention itself rather than in the object attended to. Ibn Arabi's inward turn ('clarity grows when attention returns to the knower') structurally mirrors the Śāktopāya's equation of sustained attention with knowledge—the knower's focused awareness becomes the epistemological ground.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi emphasizes negation and transcendence (what the Absolute is not), while the Śāktopāya affirms attention as an active power of consciousness; Ibn Arabi's apophatic method contrasts with Kashmir Shaivism's affirmative metaphysics of Śakti.

items.citation: Tao Te Ching — Learning Adds; the Way Subtracts
items.resonance: Both texts prescribe a reversal of ordinary cognitive habit: Ibn Arabi's inward turn away from 'passing content' parallels the Taoist practice of 'daily diminish'—a subtraction from accumulated knowledge and external focus to access a deeper principle. Both treat knowledge as requiring withdrawal rather than accumulation.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi's withdrawal aims at the transcendent Absolute beyond all things, while the Taoist diminishment aims at alignment with the immanent, natural flow of the Dào; Ibn Arabi is apophatic and theistic, the Tao Te Ching is naturalistic and non-theistic.

items.resonance: Both texts identify ignorance as a fundamental misalignment of attention: the Pratyabhijnahrdayam's 'bewilderment by one's own powers through ignorance of authorship' mirrors Ibn Arabi's point that clarity requires attention to return to the knower—both diagnose the error as attending to effects (the fivefold act, passing content) while forgetting the source (authorship, the knower).
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi frames this as a metaphysical paradox about the Absolute's transcendence, while Kashmir Shaivism frames it as recognition of one's own divine agency; Ibn Arabi emphasizes unknowability, Pratyabhijnahrdayam emphasizes self-recognition (pratyabhijñā).

items.resonance: Both texts identify a shift from discursive knowledge to a direct knowing that is itself attention or presence: Ibn Arabi rejects theoretical knowledge in favor of inward attention to the knower, while the Siva Sutra equates sustained attention itself with knowledge, making the quality of awareness the epistemic act.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi emphasizes negation (what knowing is *not*) to point toward divine encounter, while the Siva Sutra makes attention a positive metaphysical principle—consciousness recognizing itself through focused presence.

items.citation: Plotinus Enneads — Ennead VI, Tractate 9, Section 5
items.resonance: Both texts reject the discursive intellect as the path to ultimate reality: Ibn Arabi negates reason, understanding, and conjecture; Plotinus transcends the reasoning faculty to approach the Unity, recognizing that direct knowledge of the source exceeds rational comprehension.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi frames this as turning inward to the knower within; Plotinus frames it as transcendence toward the transcendent source beyond all being, emphasizing vertical ascent rather than inward return.

items.citation: Tao Te Ching — Learning Adds; the Way Subtracts
items.resonance: Both texts prescribe a reversal of the ordinary acquisitive mode: Ibn Arabi negates accumulation of theoretical knowledge and sensory input; the Tao Te Ching prescribes daily diminishment in pursuing the Way, suggesting that realization requires subtraction rather than addition.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi's negation is epistemological (rejecting false modes of knowing) and points toward divine knowledge; the Taoist diminishment is ontological and practical (reducing artifice and desire to align with natural flow).

pratibha_layers.label: Practice (Abhyasa)
pratibha_layers.body: Read this passage slowly three times. Pause for one minute and write one sentence about how to apply it today.

items.resonance: Both texts locate knowledge in the quality and direction of attention itself rather than in external content or objects. Ibn Arabi's 'no one knows Him except Himself' and the Siva Sutra's 'sustained attention is knowledge' both make attention the primary instrument and locus of knowing.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi emphasizes a reflexive turning inward toward the divine Self as the sole knower, while the Siva Sutra presents attention as a universal epistemological principle that constitutes knowledge itself, without necessarily invoking theological reflexivity.

items.resonance: Both texts describe knowledge arising through a reversal of ordinary attention: Ibn Arabi's inward turn away from 'passing content' parallels the Yoga Spandakarika's principle that the sacred tremor becomes perceptible precisely when attention shifts from distraction to ardent striving—a reorientation of the perceiving faculty itself.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi frames this as a metaphysical necessity (only the Self knows itself), while the Yoga Spandakarika frames it as a phenomenological technique (effort and angle of perception reveal what was obscured by inattention).

items.citation: Mandukya Upanishad and Gaudapada Karika — Verses 8–12 · Om and the Fourfold Correspondence
items.resonance: Both passages establish a correspondence between a subtle inner principle and a method of inquiry that transforms that principle into a complete path of self-knowledge. Ibn Arabi's inward return to the knower parallels the Mandukya's mapping of consciousness-states onto Om, making the vehicle of inquiry itself a mirror of what is sought.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi emphasizes the exclusivity and unity of the divine knower, while the Mandukya employs systematic analytical correspondence and phonetic meditation as the structural method.

title: Being Itself Conceals The Witness
thesis: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.

items.definition: Arabic tawḥīd from waḥḥada ‘to make/declare one’ → absolute oneness of the Real, radicalized here as sole agency and sole being Here: Being Itself Conceals The Witness Pearl #8 His veil is His oneness since nothing veils Him other than Him. Trap: hearing a creedal slogan rather than ontological exclusivity of wujūd
Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

items.citation: Mandukya Upanishad and Gaudapada Karika — Verse 7 · Turīya — The Fourth
items.resonance: Both texts use radical negation to point toward a non-dual reality that cannot be grasped by conceptual categories. The Mandukya's Turīya negates all states of consciousness (inward, outward, both, mass, consciousness itself) just as Ibn Arabi's 'veil is His oneness' negates all veils except the Self—each move dissolves the subject-object duality by exhausting false positions.
items.divergence: The Mandukya negates through enumeration of states to reach a fourth transcendent principle; Ibn Arabi negates through the paradox of self-veiling to reveal immediate unity, emphasizing the Sufi doctrine of annihilation (fanā') rather than the Vedantic ascent to Turīya.

items.resonance: Both passages locate liberation in direct recognition of authorship or agency: Ibn Arabi's 'nothing veils Him other than Him' mirrors the Pratyabhijnahrdayam's recognition that consciousness itself is the author of all manifestation, collapsing the veil between knower and known through self-recognition.
items.divergence: The Pratyabhijnahrdayam emphasizes the mind's ascent through introversion to Supreme Consciousness; Ibn Arabi emphasizes the paradoxical self-veiling that reveals oneness, grounding the insight in the Sufi principle that God alone is the true agent.

items.citation: Svetasvatara Upanishad — Knowledge and Ignorance in the Imperishable
items.resonance: Both texts identify the fundamental problem as a hidden duality—Ibn Arabi's veil of oneness and the Svetasvatara's 'knowledge and ignorance hidden in Brahman'—suggesting that the apparent separation between knower and known is itself the structure that must be seen through.
items.divergence: The Svetasvatara treats knowledge and ignorance as two principles to be discriminated within Brahman; Ibn Arabi treats the veil as a single paradoxical unity (His oneness itself), emphasizing non-dual recognition over dualistic discernment.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Translation
pratibha_layers.body: His own being veils Him. His being is concealed by His oneness without any condition. No one other than He sees Him. No sent prophet, perfect saint or angel brought close knows Him.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.

items.definition: Arabic tawḥīd from waḥḥada ‘to make/declare one’ → absolute oneness of the Real, radicalized here as sole agency and sole being Here: His being is concealed by His oneness without any condition. Trap: hearing a creedal slogan rather than ontological exclusivity of wujūd
Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

items.citation: Svetasvatara Upanishad — The One Hidden in All Beings
items.resonance: Both texts posit a fundamental veiling: Ibn Arabi's 'own being veils Him' mirrors the Svetasvatara's 'hidden in all beings'—each tradition locates the ultimate reality as simultaneously present and obscured by the very manifestation through which it appears.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi emphasizes the veil as ontological self-concealment (the divine nature itself conceals), while Svetasvatara frames hiddenness as a spatial or perceptual condition (the witness remains hidden *within* beings, awaiting recognition).

items.resonance: Both passages point to a direct non-dual recognition that dissolves the subject-object split: 'His own being veils Him' and 'For one who sees unity, what delusion and what sorrow remain?' both suggest that the veil *is* the illusion of separation, dissolved in immediate seeing.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi's formulation emphasizes the paradox of veiling itself as the mechanism, while Isavasya locates the shift in the *seeing* (dṛṣṭi) that recognizes unity, making knowledge rather than ontological structure the pivot.

items.citation: Astavakra Gita — Key Verses from Chapters 3–7
items.resonance: Both texts dissolve the apparent solidity of individual existence into a non-dual ground: 'His own being veils Him' parallels the recognition 'so'ham asmīti' (I am That)—the separate self-sense is revealed as the veil obscuring the singular reality.
items.divergence: Astavakra's approach is epistemological (knowledge of identity dissolves the veil), while Ibn Arabi's is metaphysical (being itself is the veiling mechanism, requiring grace rather than gnosis alone).

items.resonance: Both passages assert that ordinary perception and conceptual knowledge obstruct access to a unifying principle, and that a shift in understanding—from multiplicity to essential unity—enables perception of what is normally imperceptible.
items.divergence: Chāndogya frames this as instruction in non-dual knowledge (Brahman); Ibn Arabi frames it as the concealment of Being by Oneness itself, a metaphysical condition rather than an epistemological correction.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Translation
pratibha_layers.body: He sent Himself from Himself, through Himself to Himself. There is no intermediary or means other than Him. There is no difference between the sender, that which is sent and the one to whom it is sent. The very existence of the prophetic message is His existence.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body: The emphasis turns inward: clarity grows when attention returns to the knower rather than the passing content.

items.definition: Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: The very existence of the prophetic message is His existence. Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

Arabic tawḥīd from waḥḥada ‘to make/declare one’ → absolute oneness of the Real, radicalized here as sole agency and sole being Trap: hearing a creedal slogan rather than ontological exclusivity of wujūd

pratibha_layers.label: Practice (Abhyasa)
pratibha_layers.body: Read this passage slowly three times. Pause for one minute and write one sentence about how to apply it today.

items.resonance: Both texts make attention itself the primary instrument of knowledge: Ibn Arabi's return of attention to the knower (rather than content) structurally mirrors the Siva Sutra's equation of sustained attention with knowledge itself. In both, the shift is from what is known to the quality of knowing.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi frames this as a reflexive movement of the divine Self (Himself to Himself), while the Siva Sutra treats attention as a yogic practice accessible to the practitioner; one is metaphysical circularity, the other is methodological discipline.

items.citation: Mandukya Upanishad and Gaudapada Karika — Verses 8–12 · Om and the Fourfold Correspondence
items.resonance: Both passages establish a correspondence between an inner principle (the Self/Atman) and a mediating form (Om's four quarters, or the triadic self-sending): each uses structural analysis to map the knower onto a symbolic system that enables self-inquiry.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi's self-sending is a single reflexive act of divine consciousness, while the Mandukya uses phonetic correspondence as an analytical tool to stabilize the mind in meditation; one is ontological, the other is epistemological.

items.resonance: Both texts describe clarity arising through intensified attention directed inward: the Yoga Spandakarika's ardent striving toward the supreme tremor parallels Ibn Arabi's inward return of attention, where effort and focus dissolve obscuration.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi emphasizes the reflexive nature of attention (returning to the knower), while the Yoga Spandakarika frames it as striving toward an external-yet-inner sacred principle; the former is self-referential, the latter is devotional.

items.citation: Plotinus Enneads — Ennead V, Tractate 1, Section 12
items.resonance: Both texts locate the problem of self-knowledge in a misdirection of attention: the soul/self continuously acts or manifests, but remains unrecognized because awareness is absorbed in external content (sense-experiences, passing phenomena). Clarity requires redirecting attention inward to the source itself.
items.divergence: Plotinus frames this as a perceptual blindness within a hierarchical emanationist cosmos; Ibn Arabi's formulation collapses the distinction between knower, knowing, and known into radical non-duality, making the inward turn a dissolution of subject-object structure rather than a reorientation within it.

items.resonance: Both passages point to a recognition that occurs when attention ceases to track multiplicity and returns to undifferentiated ground: the Self manifests in the Void precisely as the collapse of sender-sent-receiver distinctions; nonduality reveals itself when the apparatus of differentiation is suspended.
items.divergence: The Vijnana Bhairava frames this as entry into a phenomenological state (the Void); Ibn Arabi's formulation is more radically metaphysical—it asserts an ontological non-difference that was always already the case, not a state to be entered.

items.definition: Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Here: There is no other, and there is no existence belonging to any other than He — nor to its ceasing to be (fanāʾ), nor to its name, nor to its named. Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: This passage stands at the heart of the treatise's teaching on the oneness of being (waḥdat al-wujūd). Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

‘unity of being/finding’ → the Real’s being is one; multiplicity is relational appearance, not rival substances Here: This passage stands at the heart of the treatise's teaching on the oneness of being (waḥdat al-wujūd). Trap: pantheist collapse that erases servant/Lord distinction

from ʿarafa ‘to know/recognize’ → gnosis as recognition of the Real’s sole agency, not informational theology Here: Self-knowledge, then, is not the annihilation of a real self but the removal of an illusion — the recognition that the only Knower who ever was is God knowing… Trap: equating mystical knowing with accumulated doctrine

‘self/soul/breath’ → the claiming self that must be known so its independence can be seen through Here: It is not meant by this that you are something that exists, or that your attributes are something that exists, but rather that you never were nor will be, whet… Trap: psychologizing as ego-therapy without ontological stakes

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Translation
pratibha_layers.body: There is no existence to any other who could pass away, or have a name or be named. Because of this, the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace, said, Whoever knows their self, knows their Lord.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body: The emphasis turns inward: clarity grows when attention returns to the knower rather than the passing content.

items.definition: Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Here: Self-Knowledge Dissolves the Illusion of Other Pearl #16 There is no existence to any other who could pass away, or have a name or be named. Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: Self-Knowledge Dissolves the Illusion of Other Pearl #16 There is no existence to any other who could pass away, or have a name or be named. Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

pratibha_layers.label: Practice (Abhyasa)
pratibha_layers.body: Read this passage slowly three times. Pause for one minute and write one sentence about how to apply it today.

items.citation: Plotinus Enneads — Ennead V, Tractate 1, Section 12
items.resonance: Both texts locate the problem in *misdirected attention*: the soul/self continuously manifests its true nature, but remains obscured because consciousness is absorbed in transient content (sense-experiences, passing phenomena). Clarity requires a reversal of attention back to the knower itself.
items.divergence: Plotinus frames this as a metaphysical fact about the soul's continuous activity; Ibn Arabi emphasizes the ontological non-existence of the 'other' (passing content), making the inward turn a recognition of what never truly was.

items.resonance: Both propose that entry into a non-dual or void state reveals the Self's true nature directly. The structural move is: dissolve the multiplicity of named/passing things, and the Self manifests as what remains—the unchanging knower.
items.divergence: Vijnana Bhairava locates this in nondual consciousness as the ground of manifestation; Ibn Arabi denies existence to the 'other' entirely, making the inward turn a negation of false attribution rather than an ascent to a higher state.

items.definition: Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Here: Second, and more subtly, the error of those who make 'ceasing to be' (fanāʾ) a precondition for knowing God. Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: This passage stands at the heart of the treatise's teaching on waḥdat al-wujūd — the oneness of being. Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

‘unity of being/finding’ → the Real’s being is one; multiplicity is relational appearance, not rival substances Here: This passage stands at the heart of the treatise's teaching on waḥdat al-wujūd — the oneness of being. Trap: pantheist collapse that erases servant/Lord distinction

from ʿarafa ‘to know/recognize’ → gnosis as recognition of the Real’s sole agency, not informational theology Here: Direct, experiential knowledge or gnosis — here, the self-knowledge that is identical with knowledge of God, since the self was never other than He. Trap: equating mystical knowing with accumulated doctrine

‘association/partnership’ → ascribing independent power or being to what is other-than-God Here: To say 'I must cease to be' still affirms that there was a real 'I' to be extinguished — and to affirm a second existence alongside God is precisely shirk (ass… Trap: narrowing to idol-worship while missing subtle self-ascription of agency

title: You Never Were, Only Awareness Remains
thesis: The emphasis turns inward: clarity grows when attention returns to the knower rather than the passing content.
source_excerpt: It is not that He enters into you or that you enter into Him, or that He comes out of you or that you come out of Him. That does not mean that you have being and you are qualified by this or that attribute. What is meant is that you never were and never will be, whether through yourself or through Him or in Him or with Him.

title: The Knower Dissolves Into Knowing Itself
thesis: The emphasis turns inward: clarity grows when attention returns to the knower rather than the passing content.
source_excerpt: That does not mean that you have being and you are qualified by this or that attribute. What is meant is that you never were and never will be, whether through yourself or through Him or in Him or with Him.
translation_literal: That does not mean that you have being and you are qualified by this or that attribute. What is meant is that you never were and never will be, whether through yourself or through Him or in Him or with Him.
commentary: The emphasis turns inward: clarity grows when attention returns to the knower rather than the passing content.

sanskrit_devanagari:
وأكثر العُرَّاف أضافوا معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء – وذلك غلط وسهو واضح: فإن معرفة الله – تعالى – لا تحتاج إلى فناء الوجود ولا إلى فناء فنائه، لأن الشيء لا وجود له، وما لا وجود له لا فناء له؛ فإن الفناء بعد إثبات الوجود. فإذا عرفت نفسك بلا وجود ولا فناء فقد عرفتَ الله. – وإلا فلا.

وفي إضافة معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وإلى فناء فنائه إثباتُ الشرك، لأنك إذا أضفت معرفة الله إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء، كان الوجود لغير الله ونقيضه – وهناك شرك واضح، لأن النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – قال: "مَن عرف نفسَه فقد عرف ربَّه"، ولم يقل: "مَن فني عن نفسه عرف ربَّه." فإن إثبات الغير يناقض فناءه، وما لا يجوز ثبوتُه لا يجوز فناؤه. وجودك لا شيء، واللاشيء لا يُضاف إلى شيء، لا فانٍ ولا غير فانٍ، ولا موجود ولا معدوم. «أنت» الآن كما كنتَ معدَمًا قبل التكوين. فالآن الأزل، والآن الأبد، والآن القِدَم. فالله هو وجود الأزل ووجود الأبد ووجود القِدَم؛ فإنه بلا وجود الأزل والأبد والقِدَم لم يكن كذلك ما كان وحده لا شريك له. وواجب أن يكون وحده لا شريك له: فإن "شريكه" هو الذي يكون وجودُه بذاته، لا بوجود الله؛ ومَن يكن كذلك لم يكن محتاجًا إليه، فيكون إذًا ربًّا ثانيًا – وذلك محال: فليس لله شريك ولا ندٌّ ولا كفؤ. ومَن رأى شيئًا مع الله أو من الله أو في الله – وذلك الشيء يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية – فقد جعل ذلك الشيء أيضًا شريكًا يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية. ومن جوَّزَ أن يكون مع الله شيءٌ يقوم بنفسه، أو يقوم به، أو هو فانٍ عن وجوده أو عن فنائه، فهو بعدُ ما شمَّ رائحة معرفة النفس، لأن مَن جوَّزَ أن يكون موجودًا سواه، قائمًا به، فيه يصير فانيًا في فنائه، فتسلسل الفناء بالفناء، – وذلك شِرْك بعد شِرْك، وليس بمعرفة النفس، – هو مُشْرِك، لا عارف بالله ولا بنفسه.
sanskrit_iast:
wa akthar al-ʿurrāf ʾaḍāfū maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa fanāʾ al-fanāʾ – wa dhālika ghalṭ wa sahw wāḍiḥ: faʾinna maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – lā taḥtāj ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa lā ilā fanāʾ fanāʾih, liʾanna al-shayʾ lā wujūd lahu, wa mā lā wujūd lahu lā fanāʾ lahu; faʾinna al-fanāʾ baʿda ʾithbāt al-wujūd. fa-idhā ʿarafta nafsak bilā wujūd wa lā fanāʾ faqad ʿarafta Allāh. – wa illā fa-lā.

wa fī ʾiḍāfat maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa ilā fanāʾ fanāʾih ʾithbāt al-shirk, liʾannak idhā ʾaḍafta maʿrifat Allāh ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa fanāʾ al-fanāʾ, kāna al-wujūd li-ghayr Allāh wa naqīḍuh – wa hunāka shirk wāḍiḥ, liʾanna al-nabī – ṣallā Allāh ʿalayh wa sallam – qāla: "man ʿarafa nafsahu faqad ʿarafa rabbahu," wa lam yaqūl: "man fanī ʿan nafsihi ʿarafa rabbahu." faʾinna ʾithbāt al-ghayr yunāqiḍ fanāʾahu, wa mā lā yajāz thubūtuh lā yajāz fanāʾuh. wujūdak lā shayʾ, wa al-lā shayʾ lā yuḍāf ilā shayʾ, lā fān wa lā ghayr fān, wa lā mawjūd wa lā maʿdūm. "anta" al-ān kamā kunta maʿdaman qabla al-takwīn. fa-al-ān al-ʾazal, wa al-ān al-ʾabad, wa al-ān al-qidam. fa-Allāh huwa wujūd al-ʾazal wa wujūd al-ʾabad wa wujūd al-qidam; fa-innahu bilā wujūd al-ʾazal wa al-ʾabad wa al-qidam lam yakun kathālika mā kāna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu. wa wājib an yakūna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu: fa-ʾinna "sharīkuhu" huwa alladhī yakūn wujūduhu bi-dhātihi, lā bi-wujūd Allāh; wa man yakun kathālika lam yakun muḥtājān ilayh, fa-yakūn idhān rabbān thānī – wa dhālika muḥāl: fa-laysa li-Allāh sharīk wa lā nadd wa lā kufūʾ. wa man rāʾa shayʾan maʿ Allāh aw min Allāh aw fī Allāh – wa dhālika al-shayʾ yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya – faqad jaʿala dhālika al-shayʾ ayḍan sharīkan yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya. wa man jawwaza an yakūna maʿ Allāh shayʾun yaqūm binafsihi, aw yaqūm bihi, aw huwa fān ʿan wujūdihi aw ʿan fanāʾih, fa-huwa baʿdū mā shamma rāʾiḥat maʿrifat al-nafs, liʾanna man jawwaza an yakūna mawjūdān siwāh, qāʾimān bihi, fīhi yaṣīr fānīan fī fanāʾih, fa-tasalsal al-fanāʾ bi-l-fanāʾ, – wa dhālika shirk baʿda shirk, wa laysa bi-maʿrifat al-nafs, – huwa mushrik, lā ʿārif bi-Allāh wa lā bi-nafsihi.

wa fī ʾiḍāfat maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa ilā fanāʾ fanāʾih ʾithbāt al-shirk, liʾannak idhā ʾaḍafta maʿrifat Allāh ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa fanāʾ al-fanāʾ, kāna al-wujūd li-ghayr Allāh wa naqīḍuh – wa hunāka shirk wāḍiḥ, liʾanna al-nabī – ṣallā Allāh ʿalayh wa sallam – qāla: "man ʿarafa nafsahu faqad ʿarafa rabbahu," wa lam yaqūl: "man fanī ʿan nafsihi ʿarafa rabbahu." faʾinna ʾithbāt al-ghayr yunāqiḍ fanāʾahu, wa mā lā yajāz thubūtuh lā yajāz fanāʾuh. wujūdak lā shayʾ, wa al-lā shayʾ lā yuḍāf ilā shayʾ, lā fān wa lā ghayr fān, wa lā mawjūd wa lā maʿdūm. "anta" al-ān kamā kunta maʿdaman qabla al-takwīn. fa-al-ān al-ʾazal, wa al-ān al-ʾabad, wa al-ān al-qidam. fa-Allāh huwa wujūd al-ʾazal wa wujūd al-ʾabad wa wujūd al-qidam; fa-innahu bilā wujūd al-ʾazal wa al-ʾabad wa al-qidam lam yakun kathālika mā kāna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu. wa wājib an yakūna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu: fa-ʾinna "sharīkuhu" huwa alladhī yakūn wujūduhu bi-dhātihi, lā bi-wujūd Allāh; wa man yakun kathālika lam yakun muḥtājān ilayh, fa-yakūn idhān rabbān thānī – wa dhālika muḥāl: fa-laysa li-Allāh sharīk wa lā nadd wa lā kufūʾ. wa man rāʾa shayʾan maʿ Allāh aw min Allāh aw fī Allāh – wa dhālika al-shayʾ yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya – faqad jaʿala dhālika al-shayʾ ayḍan sharīkan yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya. wa man jawwaza an yakūna maʿ Allāh shayʾun yaqūm binafsihi, aw yaqūm bihi, aw huwa fān ʿan wujūdihi aw ʿan fanāʾih, fa-huwa baʿdū mā shamma rāʾiḥat maʿrifat al-nafs, liʾanna man jawwaza an yakūna mawjūdān siwāh, qāʾimān bihi, fīhi yaṣīr fānīan fī fanāʾih, fa-tasalsal al-fanāʾ bi-l-fanāʾ, – wa dhālika shirk baʿda shirk, wa laysa bi-maʿrifat al-nafs, – huwa mushrik, lā ʿārif bi-Allāh wa lā bi-nafsihi.

items.definition: Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Here: For many Sufis, the spiritual path culminates in fanāʾ—the annihilation of the self—and then even the annihilation of that annihilation. Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

‘unity of being/finding’ → the Real’s being is one; multiplicity is relational appearance, not rival substances Here: Under waḥdat al-wujūd (the oneness of being), the created self never possessed real existence to begin with. Trap: pantheist collapse that erases servant/Lord distinction

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: Under waḥdat al-wujūd (the oneness of being), the created self never possessed real existence to begin with. Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world
from ʿarafa ‘to know/recognize’ → gnosis as recognition of the Real’s sole agency, not informational theology Trap: equating mystical knowing with accumulated doctrine

‘association/partnership’ → ascribing independent power or being to what is other-than-God Here: But the author regards this as a subtle idolatry (shirk). Trap: narrowing to idol-worship while missing subtle self-ascription of agency

title: Existence Dissolves When Attention Turns Inward
thesis: The emphasis turns inward: clarity grows when attention returns to the knower rather than the passing content.
source_excerpt: What is meant is that you never were and never will be, whether through yourself or through Him or in Him or with Him. You have neither ceased to be nor are you existent. You are Him and He is you, without any of these imperfections. If you know your existence in this way, then you know God, and if not, then not.
translation_literal: What is meant is that you never were and never will be, whether through yourself or through Him or in Him or with Him. You have neither ceased to be nor are you existent. You are Him and He is you, without any of these imperfections. If you know your existence in this way, then you know God, and if not, then not.
commentary: The emphasis turns inward: clarity grows when attention returns to the knower rather than the passing content.

sanskrit_devanagari:
وأكثر العُرَّاف أضافوا معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء – وذلك غلط وسهو واضح: فإن معرفة الله – تعالى – لا تحتاج إلى فناء الوجود ولا إلى فناء فنائه، لأن الشيء لا وجود له، وما لا وجود له لا فناء له؛ فإن الفناء بعد إثبات الوجود. فإذا عرفت نفسك بلا وجود ولا فناء فقد عرفتَ الله. – وإلا فلا.

وفي إضافة معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وإلى فناء فنائه إثباتُ الشرك، لأنك إذا أضفت معرفة الله إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء، كان الوجود لغير الله ونقيضه – وهناك شرك واضح، لأن النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – قال: "مَن عرف نفسَه فقد عرف ربَّه"، ولم يقل: "مَن فني عن نفسه عرف ربَّه." فإن إثبات الغير يناقض فناءه، وما لا يجوز ثبوتُه لا يجوز فناؤه. وجودك لا شيء، واللاشيء لا يُضاف إلى شيء، لا فانٍ ولا غير فانٍ، ولا موجود ولا معدوم. «أنت» الآن كما كنتَ معدَمًا قبل التكوين. فالآن الأزل، والآن الأبد، والآن القِدَم. فالله هو وجود الأزل ووجود الأبد ووجود القِدَم؛ فإنه بلا وجود الأزل والأبد والقِدَم لم يكن كذلك ما كان وحده لا شريك له. وواجب أن يكون وحده لا شريك له: فإن "شريكه" هو الذي يكون وجودُه بذاته، لا بوجود الله؛ ومَن يكن كذلك لم يكن محتاجًا إليه، فيكون إذًا ربًّا ثانيًا – وذلك محال: فليس لله شريك ولا ندٌّ ولا كفؤ. ومَن رأى شيئًا مع الله أو من الله أو في الله – وذلك الشيء يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية – فقد جعل ذلك الشيء أيضًا شريكًا يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية. ومن جوَّزَ أن يكون مع الله شيءٌ يقوم بنفسه، أو يقوم به، أو هو فانٍ عن وجوده أو عن فنائه، فهو بعدُ ما شمَّ رائحة معرفة النفس، لأن مَن جوَّزَ أن يكون موجودًا سواه، قائمًا به، فيه يصير فانيًا في فنائه، فتسلسل الفناء بالفناء، – وذلك شِرْك بعد شِرْك، وليس بمعرفة النفس، – هو مُشْرِك، لا عارف بالله ولا بنفسه.

Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: This is the practical face of waḥdat al-wujūd, the oneness of being. Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

‘unity of being/finding’ → the Real’s being is one; multiplicity is relational appearance, not rival substances Here: This is the practical face of waḥdat al-wujūd, the oneness of being. Trap: pantheist collapse that erases servant/Lord distinction

‘association/partnership’ → ascribing independent power or being to what is other-than-God Here: Balyānī argues that to speak of your existence 'ceasing' secretly grants that your existence was real in the first place—and to posit a real existence alongsid… Trap: narrowing to idol-worship while missing subtle self-ascription of agency

‘self/soul/breath’ → the claiming self that must be known so its independence can be seen through Here: And it is not meant by this that you are something that exists, or that your attributes are something that exists; rather, it is meant that you never were nor… Trap: psychologizing as ego-therapy without ontological stakes

title: Existence Dissolves Into Divine Identity
thesis: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.
source_excerpt: You have neither ceased to be nor are you existent. You are Him and He is you, without any of these imperfections. If you know your existence in this way, then you know God, and if not, then not.
translation_literal: You have neither ceased to be nor are you existent. You are Him and He is you, without any of these imperfections. If you know your existence in this way, then you know God, and if not, then not.
commentary: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.

sanskrit_devanagari: ولهذا قال – صلى الله عليه وسلم –: "عرفت ربِّي بربِّي، مَن عرف نفسَه فقد عرف ربَّه." وقال – صلى الله عليه وسلم –: "عرفت ربِّي بربِّي." أشار – صلى الله عليه وسلم – بذلك أنك لست أنت، «بل» أنت هو بلا أنت: لا هو داخل فيك ولا هو خارج منك، ولا أنت خارج منه ولا أنت داخل فيه؛ ولا بذلك أنك موجود وصفتك هكذا أبدًا: غني به. إنك ما كنت قط ولا تكون، لا بنفسك ولا فيه ولا معه، ولا أنت فانٍ ولا موجود. أنت هو، وهو أنت، بلا علَّة من هذه العلل. فإن عرفتَ وجودك بهذه الصفة فقد عرفتَ الله. – وإلا فلا.

title: Identity Without Imperfection Reveals Divine Knowledge
thesis: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.

sanskrit_devanagari:
وأكثر العُرَّاف أضافوا معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء – وذلك غلط وسهو واضح: فإن معرفة الله – تعالى – لا تحتاج إلى فناء الوجود ولا إلى فناء فنائه، لأن الشيء لا وجود له، وما لا وجود له لا فناء له؛ فإن الفناء بعد إثبات الوجود. فإذا عرفت نفسك بلا وجود ولا فناء فقد عرفتَ الله. – وإلا فلا.

وفي إضافة معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وإلى فناء فنائه إثباتُ الشرك، لأنك إذا أضفت معرفة الله إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء، كان الوجود لغير الله ونقيضه – وهناك شرك واضح، لأن النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – قال: "مَن عرف نفسَه فقد عرف ربَّه"، ولم يقل: "مَن فني عن نفسه عرف ربَّه." فإن إثبات الغير يناقض فناءه، وما لا يجوز ثبوتُه لا يجوز فناؤه. وجودك لا شيء، واللاشيء لا يُضاف إلى شيء، لا فانٍ ولا غير فانٍ، ولا موجود ولا معدوم. «أنت» الآن كما كنتَ معدَمًا قبل التكوين. فالآن الأزل، والآن الأبد، والآن القِدَم. فالله هو وجود الأزل ووجود الأبد ووجود القِدَم؛ فإنه بلا وجود الأزل والأبد والقِدَم لم يكن كذلك ما كان وحده لا شريك له. وواجب أن يكون وحده لا شريك له: فإن "شريكه" هو الذي يكون وجودُه بذاته، لا بوجود الله؛ ومَن يكن كذلك لم يكن محتاجًا إليه، فيكون إذًا ربًّا ثانيًا – وذلك محال: فليس لله شريك ولا ندٌّ ولا كفؤ. ومَن رأى شيئًا مع الله أو من الله أو في الله – وذلك الشيء يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية – فقد جعل ذلك الشيء أيضًا شريكًا يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية. ومن جوَّزَ أن يكون مع الله شيءٌ يقوم بنفسه، أو يقوم به، أو هو فانٍ عن وجوده أو عن فنائه، فهو بعدُ ما شمَّ رائحة معرفة النفس، لأن مَن جوَّزَ أن يكون موجودًا سواه، قائمًا به، فيه يصير فانيًا في فنائه، فتسلسل الفناء بالفناء، – وذلك شِرْك بعد شِرْك، وليس بمعرفة النفس، – هو مُشْرِك، لا عارف بالله ولا بنفسه.
sanskrit_iast:
wa akthar al-ʿurrāf ʾaḍāfū maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa fanāʾ al-fanāʾ – wa dhālika ghalṭ wa sahw wāḍiḥ: faʾinna maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – lā taḥtāj ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa lā ilā fanāʾ fanāʾih, liʾanna al-shayʾ lā wujūd lahu, wa mā lā wujūd lahu lā fanāʾ lahu; faʾinna al-fanāʾ baʿda ʾithbāt al-wujūd. fa-idhā ʿarafta nafsak bilā wujūd wa lā fanāʾ faqad ʿarafta Allāh. – wa illā fa-lā.

wa fī ʾiḍāfat maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa ilā fanāʾ fanāʾih ʾithbāt al-shirk, liʾannak idhā ʾaḍafta maʿrifat Allāh ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa fanāʾ al-fanāʾ, kāna al-wujūd li-ghayr Allāh wa naqīḍuh – wa hunāka shirk wāḍiḥ, liʾanna al-nabī – ṣallā Allāh ʿalayh wa sallam – qāla: "man ʿarafa nafsahu faqad ʿarafa rabbahu," wa lam yaqūl: "man fanī ʿan nafsihi ʿarafa rabbahu." faʾinna ʾithbāt al-ghayr yunāqiḍ fanāʾahu, wa mā lā yajāz thubūtuh lā yajāz fanāʾuh. wujūdak lā shayʾ, wa al-lā shayʾ lā yuḍāf ilā shayʾ, lā fān wa lā ghayr fān, wa lā mawjūd wa lā maʿdūm. "anta" al-ān kamā kunta maʿdaman qabla al-takwīn. fa-al-ān al-ʾazal, wa al-ān al-ʾabad, wa al-ān al-qidam. fa-Allāh huwa wujūd al-ʾazal wa wujūd al-ʾabad wa wujūd al-qidam; fa-innahu bilā wujūd al-ʾazal wa al-ʾabad wa al-qidam lam yakun kathālika mā kāna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu. wa wājib an yakūna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu: fa-ʾinna "sharīkuhu" huwa alladhī yakūn wujūduhu bi-dhātihi, lā bi-wujūd Allāh; wa man yakun kathālika lam yakun muḥtājān ilayh, fa-yakūn idhān rabbān thānī – wa dhālika muḥāl: fa-laysa li-Allāh sharīk wa lā nadd wa lā kufūʾ. wa man rāʾa shayʾan maʿ Allāh aw min Allāh aw fī Allāh – wa dhālika al-shayʾ yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya – faqad jaʿala dhālika al-shayʾ ayḍan sharīkan yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya. wa man jawwaza an yakūna maʿ Allāh shayʾun yaqūm binafsihi, aw yaqūm bihi, aw huwa fān ʿan wujūdihi aw ʿan fanāʾih, fa-huwa baʿdū mā shamma rāʾiḥat maʿrifat al-nafs, liʾanna man jawwaza an yakūna mawjūdān siwāh, qāʾimān bihi, fīhi yaṣīr fānīan fī fanāʾih, fa-tasalsal al-fanāʾ bi-l-fanāʾ, – wa dhālika shirk baʿda shirk, wa laysa bi-maʿrifat al-nafs, – huwa mushrik, lā ʿārif bi-Allāh wa lā bi-nafsihi.

items.definition: Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Here: The author corrects a subtle but pervasive error among spiritual seekers: the belief that one must first exist as a separate self and then annihilate that self… Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

‘unity of being/finding’ → the Real’s being is one; multiplicity is relational appearance, not rival substances Here: This passage strikes at the heart of the treatise's teaching on waḥdat al-wujūd (the oneness of being). Trap: pantheist collapse that erases servant/Lord distinction

Arabic tawḥīd from waḥḥada ‘to make/declare one’ → absolute oneness of the Real, radicalized here as sole agency and sole being Here: True tawḥīd leaves no residue of a second existence, not even in the mode of something that once was and then ceased. Trap: hearing a creedal slogan rather than ontological exclusivity of wujūd

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: This passage strikes at the heart of the treatise's teaching on waḥdat al-wujūd (the oneness of being). Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

‘self/soul/breath’ → the claiming self that must be known so its independence can be seen through Here: And it is not meant by this that you are something that exists, or that your attributes are something that exists; rather, it is meant that you never were, nor… Trap: psychologizing as ego-therapy without ontological stakes

وأكثر العُرَّاف أضافوا معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء – وذلك غلط وسهو واضح: فإن معرفة الله – تعالى – لا تحتاج إلى فناء الوجود ولا إلى فناء فنائه، لأن الشيء لا وجود له، وما لا وجود له لا فناء له؛ فإن الفناء بعد إثبات الوجود. فإذا عرفت نفسك بلا وجود ولا فناء فقد عرفتَ الله. – وإلا فلا.

وفي إضافة معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وإلى فناء فنائه إثباتُ الشرك، لأنك إذا أضفت معرفة الله إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء، كان الوجود لغير الله ونقيضه – وهناك شرك واضح، لأن النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – قال: "مَن عرف نفسَه فقد عرف ربَّه"، ولم يقل: "مَن فني عن نفسه عرف ربَّه." فإن إثبات الغير يناقض فناءه، وما لا يجوز ثبوتُه لا يجوز فناؤه. وجودك لا شيء، واللاشيء لا يُضاف إلى شيء، لا فانٍ ولا غير فانٍ، ولا موجود ولا معدوم. «أنت» الآن كما كنتَ معدَمًا قبل التكوين. فالآن الأزل، والآن الأبد، والآن القِدَم. فالله هو وجود الأزل ووجود الأبد ووجود القِدَم؛ فإنه بلا وجود الأزل والأبد والقِدَم لم يكن كذلك ما كان وحده لا شريك له. وواجب أن يكون وحده لا شريك له: فإن "شريكه" هو الذي يكون وجودُه بذاته، لا بوجود الله؛ ومَن يكن كذلك لم يكن محتاجًا إليه، فيكون إذًا ربًّا ثانيًا – وذلك محال: فليس لله شريك ولا ندٌّ ولا كفؤ. ومَن رأى شيئًا مع الله أو من الله أو في الله – وذلك الشيء يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية – فقد جعل ذلك الشيء أيضًا شريكًا يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية. ومن جوَّزَ أن يكون مع الله شيءٌ يقوم بنفسه، أو يقوم به، أو هو فانٍ عن وجوده أو عن فنائه، فهو بعدُ ما شمَّ رائحة معرفة النفس، لأن مَن جوَّزَ أن يكون موجودًا سواه، قائمًا به، فيه يصير فانيًا في فنائه، فتسلسل الفناء بالفناء، – وذلك شِرْك بعد شِرْك، وليس بمعرفة النفس، – هو مُشْرِك، لا عارف بالله ولا بنفسه.
sanskrit_iast:
wa akthar al-ʿurrāf ʾaḍāfū maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa fanāʾ al-fanāʾ – wa dhālika ghalṭ wa sahw wāḍiḥ: faʾinna maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – lā taḥtāj ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa lā ilā fanāʾ fanāʾih, liʾanna al-shayʾ lā wujūd lahu, wa mā lā wujūd lahu lā fanāʾ lahu; faʾinna al-fanāʾ baʿda ʾithbāt al-wujūd. fa-idhā ʿarafta nafsak bilā wujūd wa lā fanāʾ faqad ʿarafta Allāh. – wa illā fa-lā.

wa fī ʾiḍāfat maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa ilā fanāʾ fanāʾih ʾithbāt al-shirk, liʾannak idhā ʾaḍafta maʿrifat Allāh ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa fanāʾ al-fanāʾ, kāna al-wujūd li-ghayr Allāh wa naqīḍuh – wa hunāka shirk wāḍiḥ, liʾanna al-nabī – ṣallā Allāh ʿalayh wa sallam – qāla: "man ʿarafa nafsahu faqad ʿarafa rabbahu," wa lam yaqūl: "man fanī ʿan nafsihi ʿarafa rabbahu." faʾinna ʾithbāt al-ghayr yunāqiḍ fanāʾahu, wa mā lā yajāz thubūtuh lā yajāz fanāʾuh. wujūdak lā shayʾ, wa al-lā shayʾ lā yuḍāf ilā shayʾ, lā fān wa lā ghayr fān, wa lā mawjūd wa lā maʿdūm. "anta" al-ān kamā kunta maʿdaman qabla al-takwīn. fa-al-ān al-ʾazal, wa al-ān al-ʾabad, wa al-ān al-qidam. fa-Allāh huwa wujūd al-ʾazal wa wujūd al-ʾabad wa wujūd al-qidam; fa-innahu bilā wujūd al-ʾazal wa al-ʾabad wa al-qidam lam yakun kathālika mā kāna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu. wa wājib an yakūna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu: fa-ʾinna "sharīkuhu" huwa alladhī yakūn wujūduhu bi-dhātihi, lā bi-wujūd Allāh; wa man yakun kathālika lam yakun muḥtājān ilayh, fa-yakūn idhān rabbān thānī – wa dhālika muḥāl: fa-laysa li-Allāh sharīk wa lā nadd wa lā kufūʾ. wa man rāʾa shayʾan maʿ Allāh aw min Allāh aw fī Allāh – wa dhālika al-shayʾ yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya – faqad jaʿala dhālika al-shayʾ ayḍan sharīkan yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya. wa man jawwaza an yakūna maʿ Allāh shayʾun yaqūm binafsihi, aw yaqūm bihi, aw huwa fān ʿan wujūdihi aw ʿan fanāʾih, fa-huwa baʿdū mā shamma rāʾiḥat maʿrifat al-nafs, liʾanna man jawwaza an yakūna mawjūdān siwāh, qāʾimān bihi, fīhi yaṣīr fānīan fī fanāʾih, fa-tasalsal al-fanāʾ bi-l-fanāʾ, – wa dhālika shirk baʿda shirk, wa laysa bi-maʿrifat al-nafs, – huwa mushrik, lā ʿārif bi-Allāh wa lā bi-nafsihi.

items.definition: Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Here: The critique of 'ceasing to be' (fanāʾ) is therefore surprising and precise. Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: This is the heart of waḥdat al-wujūd, the oneness of being: there is only one true existence, God's existence, and what we take to be our own separate being is… Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

‘unity of being/finding’ → the Real’s being is one; multiplicity is relational appearance, not rival substances Here: This is the heart of waḥdat al-wujūd, the oneness of being: there is only one true existence, God's existence, and what we take to be our own separate being is… Trap: pantheist collapse that erases servant/Lord distinction

from ʿarafa ‘to know/recognize’ → gnosis as recognition of the Real’s sole agency, not informational theology Here: Direct experiential knowledge or gnosis of God; here identified with true self-knowledge — knowing that one has no existence apart from God. Trap: equating mystical knowing with accumulated doctrine

‘association/partnership’ → ascribing independent power or being to what is other-than-God Here: That hidden affirmation is itself the polytheism (shirk) the seeker meant to escape. Trap: narrowing to idol-worship while missing subtle self-ascription of agency

title: Knowledge of God Requires No Annihilation
thesis: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.
source_excerpt: Most of those who claim to know God make the knowledge of God dependent on the passing away of existence and on the passing away of that passing away. That is clearly an error and misconception.
translation_literal: Most of those who claim to know God make the knowledge of God dependent on the passing away of existence and on the passing away of that passing away. That is clearly an error and misconception.

"anta" al-ān kamā kunta maʿdaman qabla al-takwīn. fa-al-ān al-ʾazal, wa al-ān al-ʾabad, wa al-ān al-qidam. fa-Allāh huwa wujūd al-ʾazal wa wujūd al-ʾabad wa wujūd al-qidam; fa-innahu bilā wujūd al-ʾazal wa al-ʾabad wa al-qidam lam yakun kathālika mā kāna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu. wa wājib an yakūna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu: fa-ʾinna "sharīkuhu" huwa alladhī yakūn wujūduhu bi-dhātihi, lā bi-wujūd Allāh; wa man yakun kathālika lam yakun muḥtājān ilayh, fa-yakūn idhān rabbān thānī – wa dhālika muḥāl: fa-laysa li-Allāh sharīk wa lā nadd wa lā kufūʾ. wa man rāʾa shayʾan maʿ Allāh aw min Allāh aw fī Allāh – wa dhālika al-shayʾ yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya – faqad jaʿala dhālika al-shayʾ ayḍan sharīkan yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya. wa man jawwaza an yakūna maʿ Allāh shayʾun yaqūm binafsihi, aw yaqūm bihi, aw huwa fān ʿan wujūdihi aw ʿan fanāʾih, fa-huwa baʿdū mā shamma rāʾiḥat maʿrifat al-nafs, liʾanna man jawwaza an yakūna mawjūdān siwāh, qāʾimān bihi, fīhi yaṣīr fānīan fī fanāʾih, fa-tasalsal al-fanāʾ bi-l-fanāʾ, – wa dhālika shirk baʿda shirk, wa laysa bi-maʿrifat al-nafs, – huwa mushrik, lā ʿārif bi-Allāh wa lā bi-nafsihi.

pratibha_layers.label: Original (Arabic)
pratibha_layers.body:
وأكثر العُرَّاف أضافوا معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء – وذلك غلط وسهو واضح: فإن معرفة الله – تعالى – لا تحتاج إلى فناء الوجود ولا إلى فناء فنائه، لأن الشيء لا وجود له، وما لا وجود له لا فناء له؛ فإن الفناء بعد إثبات الوجود. فإذا عرفت نفسك بلا وجود ولا فناء فقد عرفتَ الله. – وإلا فلا.

وفي إضافة معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وإلى فناء فنائه إثباتُ الشرك، لأنك إذا أضفت معرفة الله إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء، كان الوجود لغير الله ونقيضه – وهناك شرك واضح، لأن النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – قال: "مَن عرف نفسَه فقد عرف ربَّه"، ولم يقل: "مَن فني عن نفسه عرف ربَّه." فإن إثبات الغير يناقض فناءه، وما لا يجوز ثبوتُه لا يجوز فناؤه. وجودك لا شيء، واللاشيء لا يُضاف إلى شيء، لا فانٍ ولا غير فانٍ، ولا موجود ولا معدوم. «أنت» الآن كما كنتَ معدَمًا قبل التكوين. فالآن الأزل، والآن الأبد، والآن القِدَم. فالله هو وجود الأزل ووجود الأبد ووجود القِدَم؛ فإنه بلا وجود الأزل والأبد والقِدَم لم يكن كذلك ما كان وحده لا شريك له. وواجب أن يكون وحده لا شريك له: فإن "شريكه" هو الذي يكون وجودُه بذاته، لا بوجود الله؛ ومَن يكن كذلك لم يكن محتاجًا إليه، فيكون إذًا ربًّا ثانيًا – وذلك محال: فليس لله شريك ولا ندٌّ ولا كفؤ. ومَن رأى شيئًا مع الله أو من الله أو في الله – وذلك الشيء يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية – فقد جعل ذلك الشيء أيضًا شريكًا يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية. ومن جوَّزَ أن يكون مع الله شيءٌ يقوم بنفسه، أو يقوم به، أو هو فانٍ عن وجوده أو عن فنائه، فهو بعدُ ما شمَّ رائحة معرفة النفس، لأن مَن جوَّزَ أن يكون موجودًا سواه، قائمًا به، فيه يصير فانيًا في فنائه، فتسلسل الفناء بالفناء، – وذلك شِرْك بعد شِرْك، وليس بمعرفة النفس، – هو مُشْرِك، لا عارف بالله ولا بنفسه.
pratibha_layers.layer_provenance: Arabic: classical text of Risālat al-Wujūdiyya / Risālat al-Aḥadiyya (Auḥad al-Dīn al-Balyānī; traditionally ascribed to Ibn ʿArabī). Unicode transcription from https://www.ibnalarabi.com/books/wujudiya.php (text pages), saved at data/raw_texts/pd/arabic/balyani_risalat_al_wujudiyya_ahadiyya_ar.txt. Passage aligned using T. H. Weir JRAS 1901 English as locator. Underlying medieval Arabic is public domain.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Translation
pratibha_layers.body: Most of those who claim to know God make the knowledge of God dependent on the passing away of existence and on the passing away of that passing away. That is clearly an error and misconception.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.

items.definition: Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Here: Knowledge of God Requires No Annihilation Pearl #26 Most of those who claim to know God make the knowledge of God dependent on the passing away of existence an… Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: Knowledge of God Requires No Annihilation Pearl #26 Most of those who claim to know God make the knowledge of God dependent on the passing away of existence an… Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

from ʿarafa ‘to know/recognize’ → gnosis as recognition of the Real’s sole agency, not informational theology Here: Let that failed effort collapse into recognition: there is no 'you' here to be extinguished, only the one existence looking through your eyes. Trap: equating mystical knowing with accumulated doctrine

pratibha_layers.label: Practice (Abhyasa)
pratibha_layers.body: Read this passage slowly three times. Pause for one minute and write one sentence about how to apply it today.

items.resonance: Both passages diagnose a false knowledge that masquerades as true knowledge: Heraclitus observes that people lack understanding of daily encounters yet believe themselves knowledgeable; Ibn Arabi identifies claimants to God-knowledge who mistake a particular epistemic procedure (annihilation of existence) for actual knowledge of God. Each text exposes a structural confusion between the appearance of knowing and genuine knowing.
items.divergence: Heraclitus locates the error in inattention to the universal Logos accessible through listening; Ibn Arabi locates it in a methodological trap where practitioners confuse the dissolution of self with access to divine knowledge, requiring a different kind of recognition.

items.resonance: Both texts point toward a knowledge that transcends ordinary cognitive categories by negating the subject-object distinction: the Upaniṣad teaches that knowing the unknowable requires understanding essential oneness; Ibn Arabi suggests that true God-knowledge requires the passing away of the knower's existence itself, dissolving the duality that sustains conventional knowing.
items.divergence: The Upaniṣad frames this as a positive instruction in non-dual perception; Ibn Arabi frames it as a critique of those who mistake the *process* of annihilation for the *knowledge* itself, emphasizing the danger of reifying the method.

title: What Never Existed Cannot Disappear
thesis: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.
source_excerpt: That is clearly an error and misconception. The knowledge of God does not require the passing away of existence or the passing away of that passing away because things have no existence and what does not exist cannot pass away.

وفي إضافة معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وإلى فناء فنائه إثباتُ الشرك، لأنك إذا أضفت معرفة الله إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء، كان الوجود لغير الله ونقيضه – وهناك شرك واضح، لأن النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – قال: "مَن عرف نفسَه فقد عرف ربَّه"، ولم يقل: "مَن فني عن نفسه عرف ربَّه." فإن إثبات الغير يناقض فناءه، وما لا يجوز ثبوتُه لا يجوز فناؤه. وجودك لا شيء، واللاشيء لا يُضاف إلى شيء، لا فانٍ ولا غير فانٍ، ولا موجود ولا معدوم. «أنت» الآن كما كنتَ معدَمًا قبل التكوين. فالآن الأزل، والآن الأبد، والآن القِدَم. فالله هو وجود الأزل ووجود الأبد ووجود القِدَم؛ فإنه بلا وجود الأزل والأبد والقِدَم لم يكن كذلك ما كان وحده لا شريك له. وواجب أن يكون وحده لا شريك له: فإن "شريكه" هو الذي يكون وجودُه بذاته، لا بوجود الله؛ ومَن يكن كذلك لم يكن محتاجًا إليه، فيكون إذًا ربًّا ثانيًا – وذلك محال: فليس لله شريك ولا ندٌّ ولا كفؤ. ومَن رأى شيئًا مع الله أو من الله أو في الله – وذلك الشيء يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية – فقد جعل ذلك الشيء أيضًا شريكًا يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية. ومن جوَّزَ أن يكون مع الله شيءٌ يقوم بنفسه، أو يقوم به، أو هو فانٍ عن وجوده أو عن فنائه، فهو بعدُ ما شمَّ رائحة معرفة النفس، لأن مَن جوَّزَ أن يكون موجودًا سواه، قائمًا به، فيه يصير فانيًا في فنائه، فتسلسل الفناء بالفناء، – وذلك شِرْك بعد شِرْك، وليس بمعرفة النفس، – هو مُشْرِك، لا عارف بالله ولا بنفسه.

pratibha_layers.label: Transliteration (ALA-LC)
pratibha_layers.body:
wa akthar al-ʿurrāf ʾaḍāfū maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa fanāʾ al-fanāʾ – wa dhālika ghalṭ wa sahw wāḍiḥ: faʾinna maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – lā taḥtāj ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa lā ilā fanāʾ fanāʾih, liʾanna al-shayʾ lā wujūd lahu, wa mā lā wujūd lahu lā fanāʾ lahu; faʾinna al-fanāʾ baʿda ʾithbāt al-wujūd. fa-idhā ʿarafta nafsak bilā wujūd wa lā fanāʾ faqad ʿarafta Allāh. – wa illā fa-lā.

wa fī ʾiḍāfat maʿrifat Allāh – taʿālā – ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa ilā fanāʾ fanāʾih ʾithbāt al-shirk, liʾannak idhā ʾaḍafta maʿrifat Allāh ilā fanāʾ al-wujūd wa fanāʾ al-fanāʾ, kāna al-wujūd li-ghayr Allāh wa naqīḍuh – wa hunāka shirk wāḍiḥ, liʾanna al-nabī – ṣallā Allāh ʿalayh wa sallam – qāla: "man ʿarafa nafsahu faqad ʿarafa rabbahu," wa lam yaqūl: "man fanī ʿan nafsihi ʿarafa rabbahu." faʾinna ʾithbāt al-ghayr yunāqiḍ fanāʾahu, wa mā lā yajāz thubūtuh lā yajāz fanāʾuh. wujūdak lā shayʾ, wa al-lā shayʾ lā yuḍāf ilā shayʾ, lā fān wa lā ghayr fān, wa lā mawjūd wa lā maʿdūm. "anta" al-ān kamā kunta maʿdaman qabla al-takwīn. fa-al-ān al-ʾazal, wa al-ān al-ʾabad, wa al-ān al-qidam. fa-Allāh huwa wujūd al-ʾazal wa wujūd al-ʾabad wa wujūd al-qidam; fa-innahu bilā wujūd al-ʾazal wa al-ʾabad wa al-qidam lam yakun kathālika mā kāna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu. wa wājib an yakūna waḥdahu lā sharīk lahu: fa-ʾinna "sharīkuhu" huwa alladhī yakūn wujūduhu bi-dhātihi, lā bi-wujūd Allāh; wa man yakun kathālika lam yakun muḥtājān ilayh, fa-yakūn idhān rabbān thānī – wa dhālika muḥāl: fa-laysa li-Allāh sharīk wa lā nadd wa lā kufūʾ. wa man rāʾa shayʾan maʿ Allāh aw min Allāh aw fī Allāh – wa dhālika al-shayʾ yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya – faqad jaʿala dhālika al-shayʾ ayḍan sharīkan yaḥtāj ilā Allāh bi-l-rubūbiyya. wa man jawwaza an yakūna maʿ Allāh shayʾun yaqūm binafsihi, aw yaqūm bihi, aw huwa fān ʿan wujūdihi aw ʿan fanāʾih, fa-huwa baʿdū mā shamma rāʾiḥat maʿrifat al-nafs, liʾanna man jawwaza an yakūna mawjūdān siwāh, qāʾimān bihi, fīhi yaṣīr fānīan fī fanāʾih, fa-tasalsal al-fanāʾ bi-l-fanāʾ, – wa dhālika shirk baʿda shirk, wa laysa bi-maʿrifat al-nafs, – huwa mushrik, lā ʿārif bi-Allāh wa lā bi-nafsihi.

items.definition: Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Here: The author critiques the widespread doctrine that liberating knowledge (maʿrifa) requires fanāʾ — the 'passing away' or annihilation of the self — and even the… Trap: self-erasure as quietism or dissociation rather than clearing of false independence

Arabic wujūd ‘finding/being found; existence’ → being as what is found in God alone; creatures have no independent wujūd Here: Here understood in its most radical sense (waḥdat al-wujūd): only God's existence is real, and nothing exists alongside Him. Trap: treating ‘existence’ as a neutral metaphysical predicate shared equally by God and world

‘unity of being/finding’ → the Real’s being is one; multiplicity is relational appearance, not rival substances Here: Here understood in its most radical sense (waḥdat al-wujūd): only God's existence is real, and nothing exists alongside Him. Trap: pantheist collapse that erases servant/Lord distinction

Arabic tawḥīd from waḥḥada ‘to make/declare one’ → absolute oneness of the Real, radicalized here as sole agency and sole being Here: But from the standpoint of pure tawḥīd (oneness of being), only God truly is; the self and all created things have no independent existence to begin with. Trap: hearing a creedal slogan rather than ontological exclusivity of wujūd

‘self/soul/breath’ → the claiming self that must be known so its independence can be seen through Here: So if you know yourself without existence or ceasing to be, then you know God; and if not, then not. Trap: psychologizing as ego-therapy without ontological stakes

title: What Never Existed Cannot Dissolve
thesis: Read this line as a contemplative pointer: pause interpretation for a moment and let the insight disclose itself directly.
source_excerpt: The knowledge of God does not require the passing away of existence or the passing away of that passing away because things have no existence and what does not exist cannot pass away. Passing away implies the prior existence of the thing that passes away.
translation_literal: The knowledge of God does not require the passing away of existence or the passing away of that passing away because things have no existence and what does not exist cannot pass away. Passing away implies the prior existence of the thing that passes away.

items.definition: Arabic fanāʾ ‘passing away, evanescence’ → passing-away of the egoic claim before the Real Here: Many spiritual seekers imagine the goal is fanāʾ—the annihilation or 'passing away' of the self—and then even the annihilation of that annihilation. Arabic tawḥīd from waḥḥada ‘to make/declare one’ → absolute oneness of the Real, radicalized here as sole agency and sole being Here: True tawḥīd, the passage insists, does not require you to destroy something that never was. title: Knowledge of God Requires Annihilation of Self
thesis: The emphasis turns inward: clarity grows when attention returns to the knower rather than the passing content.
source_excerpt: Passing away implies the prior existence of the thing that passes away. If you know yourself without existing and passing away, then you know God, and if not, then not. By making the knowledge of God dependent on the passing away of your existence and the passing away of that passing away, there is an affirmation of something other than God.
translation_literal: Passing away implies the prior existence of the thing that passes away. If you know yourself without existing and passing away, then you know God, and if not, then not. By making the knowledge of God dependent on the passing away of your existence and the passing away of that passing away, there is an affirmation of something other than God.
commentary: The emphasis turns inward: clarity grows when attention returns to the knower rather than the passing content.

sanskrit_devanagari:
وأكثر العُرَّاف أضافوا معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء – وذلك غلط وسهو واضح: فإن معرفة الله – تعالى – لا تحتاج إلى فناء الوجود ولا إلى فناء فنائه، لأن الشيء لا وجود له، وما لا وجود له لا فناء له؛ فإن الفناء بعد إثبات الوجود. فإذا عرفت نفسك بلا وجود ولا فناء فقد عرفتَ الله. – وإلا فلا.

وفي إضافة معرفة الله – تعالى – إلى فناء الوجود وإلى فناء فنائه إثباتُ الشرك، لأنك إذا أضفت معرفة الله إلى فناء الوجود وفناء الفناء، كان الوجود لغير الله ونقيضه – وهناك شرك واضح، لأن النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – قال: "مَن عرف نفسَه فقد عرف ربَّه"، ولم يقل: "مَن فني عن نفسه عرف ربَّه." فإن إثبات الغير يناقض فناءه، وما لا يجوز ثبوتُه لا يجوز فناؤه. وجودك لا شيء، واللاشيء لا يُضاف إلى شيء، لا فانٍ ولا غير فانٍ، ولا موجود ولا معدوم. «أنت» الآن كما كنتَ معدَمًا قبل التكوين. فالآن الأزل، والآن الأبد، والآن القِدَم. فالله هو وجود الأزل ووجود الأبد ووجود القِدَم؛ فإنه بلا وجود الأزل والأبد والقِدَم لم يكن كذلك ما كان وحده لا شريك له. وواجب أن يكون وحده لا شريك له: فإن "شريكه" هو الذي يكون وجودُه بذاته، لا بوجود الله؛ ومَن يكن كذلك لم يكن محتاجًا إليه، فيكون إذًا ربًّا ثانيًا – وذلك محال: فليس لله شريك ولا ندٌّ ولا كفؤ. ومَن رأى شيئًا مع الله أو من الله أو في الله – وذلك الشيء يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية – فقد جعل ذلك الشيء أيضًا شريكًا يحتاج إلى الله بالربوبية. ومن جوَّزَ أن يكون مع الله شيءٌ يقوم بنفسه، أو يقوم به، أو هو فانٍ عن وجوده أو عن فنائه، فهو بعدُ ما شمَّ رائحة معرفة النفس، لأن مَن جوَّزَ أن يكون موجودًا سواه، قائمًا به، فيه يصير فانيًا في فنائه، فتسلسل الفناء بالفناء، – وذلك شِرْك بعد شِرْك، وليس بمعرفة النفس، – هو مُشْرِك، لا عارف بالله ولا بنفسه.

items.citation: Plotinus Enneads — Ennead VI, Tractate 9, Section 7
items.resonance: Both texts locate knowledge through a reorientation of attention: the Sufi passage identifies clarity by turning inward to the knower (away from passing content), while Plotinus prescribes turning inward to perceive the Unity that is always present but obscured by outward focus. Each makes the same structural move—knowledge requires redirecting attention from the external to the source of perception itself.
items.divergence: Ibn Arabi grounds this inward turn in the metaphysics of passing away (fanā), a dissolution of the phenomenal self, whereas Plotinus grounds it in the soul's continuous activity that merely awaits recognition, a difference between annihilation and unveiling.

items.resonance: Both equate sustained or focused attention with knowledge itself rather than treating attention as a mere tool for acquiring knowledge. The Siva Sutra's 'Sustained attention is knowledge' and the Ibn Arabi passage's emphasis on clarity through returned attention both collapse the distinction between the act of attending and the state of knowing.
items.divergence: The Siva Sutra operates within a non-dual Kashmiri Shaivism where attention and consciousness are ontologically identical, while Ibn Arabi's framework emphasizes the knower's self-recognition through the dissolution of what passes away, a more explicitly phenomenological reversal.
